# App Roles

**A Trip Treasurer** is a person in a travel group who ends up holding all the
receipts. Think of the driver on a road trip where a friend joins mid-way in
Faisalabad: the first leg is split between two people, the rest between four,
different people pay for fuel, food and accommodation at different stops, and
at the end everyone looks to one person to work out who owes whom. They need a
fast, correct answer that the whole group will trust.

They can: add and manage trip participants (add, rename, remove); add, edit
and delete expenses, each with a description, a total amount in whole rupees,
a designated payer (who does not have to share the expense), and the subset of
participants splitting it; attach an optional tip to any expense as a
percentage or a flat rupee amount; view a settlement summary showing the
transfers needed to clear all balances; view a per-person breakdown showing
each participant's expenses, their share of each, what they personally paid,
and their resulting net balance; and start a new trip, clearing all saved data
after an explicit confirmation. Their data is saved in the browser and survives
tab closure and browser restarts on the same device.

They must never: see a settlement where the listed transfers do not account for
every rupee of every net balance; see shares on an expense that do not sum to
the expense total including tip; lose entered data without an explicit
confirmation step; remove a participant who is named on one or more expenses —
the app blocks the removal and tells the user which expenses must be updated
first; submit an expense with no participants sharing it; enter a zero or
negative expense amount; add a participant with an empty or duplicate name;
enter any monetary value — expense amount or tip — that is not a whole number of rupees (e.g. Rs. 99.50 is rejected);
enter a single expense amount above Rs. 10,000,000 (1 crore) — this cap sits
well above any realistic group expense and keeps all arithmetic within
JavaScript's safe integer range, preventing scientific notation or silent
rounding errors in any displayed result; or enter a negative tip, or a
percentage tip above 100% — the 100% ceiling blocks accidental typos such as
typing 150 instead of 15 while still accommodating any realistic generosity.

---

*There is one role because the one-off dinner bill — one expense, everyone
present, one payer — is a degenerate case of the trip. The same participant
list, expense entry, and settlement logic handle it without any additional
capability. A separate Dinner Splitter role would describe the same person
doing the same job on a smaller scale.*

# Jobs To Be Done

**J-1 (Trip Treasurer):** When a group member pays for a shared expense during
a trip where people join or leave along the way, I want to note what was spent,
who paid, and which members were sharing that particular cost, so I have a
complete account of every transaction by the time the trip ends.

**J-2 (Trip Treasurer):** When expenses are split among different subsets of
the group — some covering the full party, others only the people present for
that leg — I want every person's total to reflect only the costs they were
actually part of, so nobody pays for a stretch of the trip they weren't on and
nobody subsidises expenses that weren't theirs.

**J-3 (Trip Treasurer):** When I know everyone's net position, I want to work
out a set of transfers that clears all the debts, so the group can settle up
without anyone having to chase payments from multiple people or make more
transactions than necessary.

**J-4 (Trip Treasurer):** When a group member challenges a figure or says the
split doesn't seem right, I want to show exactly which expenses contributed to
their total, so the group accepts the result without argument and no one has to
take my word for it.

1→# User Stories
     2→
     3→*All stories have status: Not implemented. Statuses are updated after each
     4→story is built and verified against its acceptance criteria.*
     5→
     6→---
     7→
     8→## S-1 — Add a participant
     9→**Serves:** J-1 | **Status:** Not implemented
    10→
    11→As a Trip Treasurer, I want to add a named participant to the trip, so that
    12→they can be assigned as payers or included in expense splits.
    13→
    14→- Given an empty roster, when I type "Ali" and confirm, then "Ali" appears
    15→  in the participant list.
    16→- Given "Ali" is already in the roster, when I add "Sara", then both appear
    17→  in the list.
    18→- Given the add-participant form, when I submit an empty name (or a name of
    19→  only spaces), then the form shows "Name cannot be empty" and no participant
    20→  is added.
    21→- Given "Ali" is in the roster, when I try to add "Ali" (same name,
    22→  case-insensitive), then the form shows "A participant named Ali already
    23→  exists" and no duplicate is added.
    24→- Given the form shows an error, when I enter a valid unique name and confirm,
    25→  then the participant is added and the error clears.
    26→
    27→---
    28→
    29→## S-2 — Rename a participant
    30→**Serves:** J-1 | **Status:** Not implemented
    31→
    32→As a Trip Treasurer, I want to rename a participant, so that I can correct a
    33→typo or name change without losing their expense data.
    34→
    35→- Given "Ali" is in the roster, when I rename them to "Ali Khan" and confirm,
    36→  then "Ali Khan" appears in the list and all expenses that referenced "Ali"
    37→  now reference "Ali Khan".
    38→- Given the rename form, when I submit an empty name, then the form shows
    39→  "Name cannot be empty" and the name is unchanged.
    40→- Given "Ali" and "Sara" are in the roster, when I rename "Ali" to "Sara",
    41→  then the form shows "A participant named Sara already exists" and the name
    42→  is unchanged.
    43→- Given "Ali" is in the roster, when I rename "Ali" to "Ali" (no change),
    44→  then the form is accepted without error.
    45→- Given the form shows an error, when I enter a valid unique name and confirm,
    46→  then the rename succeeds and the error clears.
    47→
    48→---
    49→
    50→## S-3 — Remove a participant
    51→**Serves:** J-1 | **Status:** Not implemented
    52→
    53→As a Trip Treasurer, I want to remove a participant from the trip, so that I
    54→can correct mistakes in the group setup.
    55→
    56→- Given "Ali" is in the roster and not named on any expense (neither as payer
    57→  nor sharer), when I remove "Ali", then "Ali" no longer appears in the
    58→  participant list.
    59→- Given "Ali" is a sharer on "Fuel to Faisalabad", when I try to remove
    60→  "Ali", then the app shows "Cannot remove Ali: they appear on Fuel to
    61→  Faisalabad. Update that expense first." and Ali remains in the roster.
    62→- Given "Ali" is the payer on "Snacks" but not a sharer on that expense, when
    63→  I try to remove "Ali", then the app shows "Cannot remove Ali: they appear on
    64→  Snacks. Update that expense first." and Ali remains.
    65→- Given "Ali" appears on both "Fuel" and "Hotel", when I try to remove "Ali",
    66→  then the message lists both: "Cannot remove Ali: they appear on Fuel and
    67→  Hotel. Update those expenses first."
    68→- Given Ali has been removed from all expenses they were named on, when I
    69→  remove "Ali", then the removal succeeds.
    70→
    71→---
    72→
    73→## S-4 — Add an expense
    74→**Serves:** J-1, J-2 | **Status:** Not implemented
    75→
    76→As a Trip Treasurer, I want to add an expense with a description, total
    77→amount, payer, and the subset of participants sharing it, so that I can record
    78→exactly what was spent, who paid, and which members the cost applies to.
    79→
    80→**Normal cases:**
    81→- Given participants Ali, Sara, Bilal; when I save "Fuel" Rs. 900, paid by
    82→  Ali, shared by Ali and Sara; then the expense shows description "Fuel",
    83→  amount Rs. 900, payer Ali, sharers Ali and Sara.
    84→- Given participants Ali, Sara, Bilal; when I save "Snacks" Rs. 300, paid by
    85→  Ali, shared by Sara and Bilal (Ali is payer but not a sharer); then the
    86→  expense is saved with Ali as payer and Sara and Bilal as the only sharers.
    87→
    88→**Invalid input:**
    89→- Given the form, when I submit with no description, then the form shows
    90→  "Description cannot be empty" and no expense is saved.
    91→- Given the form, when I enter amount 0, then the form shows "Amount must be
    92→  greater than zero".
    93→- Given the form, when I enter a negative amount (e.g. −500), then the form
    94→  shows "Amount must be greater than zero".
    95→- Given the form, when I enter 999.50, then the form shows "Amount must be a
    96→  whole number of rupees".
    97→- Given the form, when I select zero sharers, then the form shows "At least
    98→  one participant must share this expense".
    99→- Given the form, when I submit without selecting a payer, then the form shows
   100→  "A payer must be selected".
   101→
   102→**Boundary values:**
   103→- Given the form, when I enter 1 (minimum valid amount), then the expense is
   104→  saved.
   105→- Given the form, when I enter Rs. 10,000,000, then the expense is saved.
   106→- Given the form, when I enter Rs. 10,000,001, then the form shows "Amount
   107→  cannot exceed Rs. 10,000,000".
   108→
   109→**Large numbers:**
   110→- Given Rs. 10,000,000 shared equally among 3 participants; when saved; then
   111→  all shares display as whole-rupee figures and no value is shown in scientific
   112→  notation.
   113→
   114→**Continuation after error:**
   115→- Given the form shows a validation error, when I correct all fields and
   116→  resubmit, then the expense is saved and the error clears.
   117→
   118→*(How shares are divided into whole rupees: see S-12. S-4 applies that rule;
   119→it is not repeated here.)*
   120→
   121→---
   122→
   123→## S-5 — Add a tip to an expense
   124→**Serves:** J-1, J-2 | **Status:** Not implemented
   125→
   126→As a Trip Treasurer, I want to attach a tip to an expense as a whole
   127→percentage or a flat rupee amount, so that the full amount actually paid is
   128→included in each participant's share.
   129→
   130→**Normal cases:**
   131→- Given "Dinner" Rs. 1,000, tip 10%, shared equally by Ali and Sara; when
   132→  saved; then total is Rs. 1,100 and each share is Rs. 550.
   133→- Given "Dinner" Rs. 1,000, flat tip Rs. 100, shared equally by Ali and Sara;
   134→  when saved; then total is Rs. 1,100 and each share is Rs. 550.
   135→- Given "Fuel" Rs. 800, tip field left blank; when saved; then total is
   136→  Rs. 800 (no tip applied).
   137→- Given "Lunch" Rs. 600, tip 10%, shared by Ali and Sara but not Bilal; when
   138→  saved; then total is Rs. 660, Ali Rs. 330, Sara Rs. 330, and Bilal owes
   139→  nothing for this expense. *(Fairness: tip follows the sharers, not the
   140→  whole group.)*
   141→
   142→**Percentage tip rounding:**
   143→- Given "Dinner" Rs. 1,235, tip 10%; the computed tip is Rs. 123.5, which
   144→  rounds up to Rs. 124 (halves round up); total is Rs. 1,359.
   145→- Given "Dinner" Rs. 1,234, tip 10%; the computed tip is Rs. 123.4, which
   146→  rounds down to Rs. 123; total is Rs. 1,357.
   147→
   148→**Invalid input:**
   149→- Given the form, when I enter a flat tip of −50, then the form shows "Tip
   150→  cannot be negative".
   151→- Given the form, when I enter −10%, then the form shows "Tip cannot be
   152→  negative".
   153→- Given the form, when I enter 101%, then the form shows "Tip percentage
   154→  cannot exceed 100%".
   155→- Given the form, when I enter a flat tip of 99.50, then the form shows "Tip
   156→  must be a whole number of rupees".
   157→
   158→**Boundary values:**
   159→- Given Rs. 500, tip exactly 100%; when saved; total is Rs. 1,000 and the
   160→  expense is accepted.
   161→- Given Rs. 500, tip 0%; when saved; total is Rs. 500.
   162→
   163→**Tip causes total to exceed cap:**
   164→- Given base Rs. 9,500,000 and flat tip Rs. 600,000 (total Rs. 10,100,000);
   165→  then the form shows "Total including tip cannot exceed Rs. 10,000,000".
   166→- Given base Rs. 9,500,000 and flat tip Rs. 500,000 (total Rs. 10,000,000);
   167→  then the expense is saved.
   168→
   169→*(Rounding when the tipped total is not evenly divisible: see S-12.)*
   170→
   171→---
   172→
   173→## S-6 — Edit an expense
   174→**Serves:** J-1, J-2 | **Status:** Not implemented
   175→
   176→As a Trip Treasurer, I want to edit a saved expense, so that I can correct
   177→amounts, payers or participant lists after initial entry.
   178→
   179→- Given expense "Fuel" Rs. 600; when I change the amount to Rs. 700 and save;
   180→  then the expense shows Rs. 700.
   181→- Given expense "Hotel" shared by Ali and Sara; when I change the sharers to
   182→  Ali, Sara, and Bilal; then the expense shows three sharers.
   183→- Given expense "Fuel" with payer Ali; when I change the payer to Sara; then
   184→  the expense shows Sara as payer.
   185→- Given the edit form; when I submit invalid input (zero amount, decimal,
   186→  above cap, no sharers, invalid tip); then the same error messages as in S-4
   187→  and S-5 apply and the original expense data is preserved.
   188→- Given the settlement summary is displayed; when I save an edit; then the
   189→  settlement recalculates automatically.
   190→
   191→---
   192→
   193→## S-7 — Delete an expense
   194→**Serves:** J-1 | **Status:** Not implemented
   195→
   196→As a Trip Treasurer, I want to delete an expense, so that I can remove entries
   197→added by mistake.
   198→
   199→- Given expense "Snacks" Rs. 200; when I choose to delete it and confirm; then
   200→  "Snacks" no longer appears in the expense list.
   201→- Given I tap delete on an expense; then the app prompts for confirmation
   202→  before removing it — a single accidental tap does not delete the expense.
   203→- Given I tap delete and then cancel at the confirmation prompt; then the
   204→  expense remains unchanged.
   205→- Given the settlement summary is displayed and I delete an expense and
   206→  confirm; then the settlement recalculates automatically.
   207→
   208→---
   209→
   210→## S-8 — Persist trip data in the browser
   211→**Serves:** J-1 | **Status:** Not implemented
   212→
   213→As a Trip Treasurer, I want the trip data to save automatically in my browser,
   214→so that I can close the tab or restart the browser at any point during a
   215→multi-day trip without losing any entered data.
   216→
   217→- Given I have added participants Ali, Sara and expense "Fuel" Rs. 600; when I
   218→  close the tab and reopen the app in the same browser on the same device;
   219→  then Ali, Sara and "Fuel" Rs. 600 are still present.
   220→- Given I have entered trip data; when I restart the browser and reopen the
   221→  app; then all participants and expenses are restored exactly as entered.
   222→- Given I add or edit an expense; then the change is saved immediately — no
   223→  manual "save trip" action is required.
   224→- Given the app is opened for the first time (no data in localStorage); then
   225→  the app starts with an empty trip and shows no error or message.
   226→- Given localStorage contains data for this app that cannot be parsed (e.g.
   227→  the storage was corrupted); then the app shows "Your saved trip data could
   228→  not be loaded. Starting a new trip." and starts with an empty trip rather
   229→  than crashing or silently discarding the data.
   230→
   231→---
   232→
   233→## S-9 — Start a new trip
   234→**Serves:** J-1 | **Status:** Not implemented
   235→
   236→As a Trip Treasurer, I want to clear all current trip data and start fresh,
   237→so that I can use the app for a new trip without previous data interfering.
   238→
   239→- Given the trip has participants and expenses; when I choose "Start new trip"
   240→  and confirm; then the participant list and expense list are both empty and
   241→  localStorage is cleared.
   242→- Given I choose "Start new trip"; when I cancel at the confirmation prompt;
   243→  then all participants and expenses remain intact.
   244→- Given the trip is already empty; when I choose "Start new trip" and confirm;
   245→  then the app remains on an empty state with no error.
   246→
   247→---
   248→
   249→## S-10 — View the settlement summary
   250→**Serves:** J-3 | **Status:** Not implemented
   251→
   252→As a Trip Treasurer, I want to see a labelled list of transfers that clears
   253→all balances, so that the group knows exactly who pays whom and the trip is
   254→fully settled.
   255→
   256→**Normal cases:**
   257→- Given Ali paid Rs. 600 for "Fuel" shared equally by Ali and Sara (each
   258→  Rs. 300); then the settlement shows "Sara pays Ali Rs. 300".
   259→- Given the Faisalabad scenario:
   260→  - "Fuel to Faisalabad" Rs. 1,500, paid by Ali, shared by Ali and Usman
   261→    (Rs. 750 each, no rounding)
   262→  - "Fuel onwards" Rs. 2,000, paid by Usman, shared by Ali, Usman, Sara,
   263→    Bilal (Rs. 500 each, no rounding)
   264→  - "Hotel" Rs. 3,001, paid by Sara, shared by Ali, Usman, Sara, Bilal
   265→    (Sara is payer and sharer — Sara Rs. 751, others Rs. 750 each per S-12)
   266→
   267→  Net balances: Ali −Rs. 500, Usman Rs. 0, Sara +Rs. 1,750,
   268→  Bilal −Rs. 1,250.
   269→
   270→  Then the settlement shows: "Bilal pays Sara Rs. 1,250" and
   271→  "Ali pays Sara Rs. 500".
   272→
   273→- Given all net balances are zero; then the settlement shows "All balances
   274→  are settled — no transfers needed."
   275→- Given only one participant exists; then the settlement shows "All balances
   276→  are settled — no transfers needed."
   277→
   278→**Empty state:**
   279→- Given no expenses have been added; when I view the settlement; then the app
   280→  shows "No expenses have been added yet."
   281→
   282→**Algorithm label:**
   283→- The settlement section is headed "Simplified settlement" (not "Minimum
   284→  transfers") to reflect that the greedy algorithm is not guaranteed to be
   285→  the mathematical minimum.
   286→
   287→**Mathematical invariant (verified by automated tests):**
   288→- Given any set of valid expenses; when the settlement is computed; then
   289→  applying all listed transfers to participants' net balances brings every
   290→  balance to exactly Rs. 0.
   291→
   292→**Continuation:**
   293→- Given the settlement is displayed; when I add, edit or delete an expense;
   294→  then the settlement recalculates automatically.
   295→
   296→---
   297→
   298→## S-11 — View the per-person breakdown
   299→**Serves:** J-2, J-4 | **Status:** Not implemented
   300→
   301→As a Trip Treasurer, I want to see a breakdown for each participant showing
   302→the expenses they shared, their share of each, what they personally paid, and
   303→their net balance, so that any group member can verify their own figure without
   304→argument.
   305→
   306→**Normal cases:**
   307→- Given Ali paid Rs. 600 for "Fuel" (shared Ali, Sara — each Rs. 300), and
   308→  Sara paid Rs. 900 for "Hotel" (shared Ali, Sara, Bilal — each Rs. 300);
   309→  Ali's breakdown shows:
   310→  - "Fuel": share Rs. 300, paid Rs. 600 → net from this expense: +Rs. 300
   311→  - "Hotel": share Rs. 300, paid Rs. 0 → net from this expense: −Rs. 300
   312→  - Summary: total paid Rs. 600, total owed Rs. 600, net balance Rs. 0
   313→- Given Bilal was not on "Fuel"; then "Fuel" does not appear in Bilal's
   314→  breakdown.
   315→- Given Ali paid Rs. 300 for "Snacks" shared by Sara and Bilal only (Ali is
   316→  payer but not a sharer); Ali's breakdown shows "Snacks": paid Rs. 300,
   317→  share Rs. 0, net from this expense +Rs. 300.
   318→
   319→**Consistency with settlement:**
   320→- Given both the per-person breakdown and the settlement summary are
   321→  displayed; then each participant's net balance in the breakdown matches
   322→  exactly the net balance used in the settlement calculation.
   323→
   324→**Zero balance:**
   325→- Given a participant's total paid equals their total owed; then their
   326→  breakdown shows net balance Rs. 0 and they do not appear in the settlement
   327→  transfers.
   328→
   329→*(Share values in the breakdown use the same rounded whole-rupee figures
   330→defined in S-12.)*
   331→
   332→---
   333→
   334→## S-12 — See how each expense's shares were rounded
   335→**Serves:** J-2, J-4 | **Status:** Not implemented
   336→
   337→As a Trip Treasurer, I want to see, for each expense, how the total was
   338→divided into whole-rupee shares and who absorbed the leftover, so that any
   339→participant can confirm the rounding was consistent and fair.
   340→

# User Stories

*All stories have status: Not implemented. Statuses are updated after each
story is built and verified against its acceptance criteria.*

---

## S-1 — Add a participant
**Serves:** J-1 | **Status:** Not implemented

As a Trip Treasurer, I want to add a named participant to the trip, so that
they can be assigned as payers or included in expense splits.

- Given an empty roster, when I type "Ali" and confirm, then "Ali" appears
  in the participant list.
- Given "Ali" is already in the roster, when I add "Sara", then both appear
  in the list.
- Given the add-participant form, when I submit an empty name (or a name of
  only spaces), then the form shows "Name cannot be empty" and no participant
  is added.
- Given "Ali" is in the roster, when I try to add "Ali" (same name,
  case-insensitive), then the form shows "A participant named Ali already
  exists" and no duplicate is added.
- Given the form shows an error, when I enter a valid unique name and confirm,
  then the participant is added and the error clears.

---

## S-2 — Rename a participant
**Serves:** J-1 | **Status:** Not implemented

As a Trip Treasurer, I want to rename a participant, so that I can correct a
typo or name change without losing their expense data.

- Given "Ali" is in the roster, when I rename them to "Ali Khan" and confirm,
  then "Ali Khan" appears in the list and all expenses that referenced "Ali"
  now reference "Ali Khan".
- Given the rename form, when I submit an empty name, then the form shows
  "Name cannot be empty" and the name is unchanged.
- Given "Ali" and "Sara" are in the roster, when I rename "Ali" to "Sara",
  then the form shows "A participant named Sara already exists" and the name
  is unchanged.
- Given "Ali" is in the roster, when I rename "Ali" to "Ali" (no change),
  then the form is accepted without error.
- Given the form shows an error, when I enter a valid unique name and confirm,
  then the rename succeeds and the error clears.

---

## S-3 — Remove a participant
**Serves:** J-1 | **Status:** Not implemented

As a Trip Treasurer, I want to remove a participant from the trip, so that I
can correct mistakes in the group setup.

- Given "Ali" is in the roster and not named on any expense (neither as payer
  nor sharer), when I remove "Ali", then "Ali" no longer appears in the
  participant list.
- Given "Ali" is a sharer on "Fuel to Faisalabad", when I try to remove
  "Ali", then the app shows "Cannot remove Ali: they appear on Fuel to
  Faisalabad. Update that expense first." and Ali remains in the roster.
- Given "Ali" is the payer on "Snacks" but not a sharer on that expense, when
  I try to remove "Ali", then the app shows "Cannot remove Ali: they appear on
  Snacks. Update that expense first." and Ali remains.
- Given "Ali" appears on both "Fuel" and "Hotel", when I try to remove "Ali",
  then the message lists both: "Cannot remove Ali: they appear on Fuel and
  Hotel. Update those expenses first."
- Given Ali has been removed from all expenses they were named on, when I
  remove "Ali", then the removal succeeds.

---

## S-4 — Add an expense
**Serves:** J-1, J-2 | **Status:** Not implemented

As a Trip Treasurer, I want to add an expense with a description, total
amount, payer, and the subset of participants sharing it, so that I can record
exactly what was spent, who paid, and which members the cost applies to.

**Normal cases:**
- Given participants Ali, Sara, Bilal; when I save "Fuel" Rs. 900, paid by
  Ali, shared by Ali and Sara; then the expense shows description "Fuel",
  amount Rs. 900, payer Ali, sharers Ali and Sara.
- Given participants Ali, Sara, Bilal; when I save "Snacks" Rs. 300, paid by
  Ali, shared by Sara and Bilal (Ali is payer but not a sharer); then the
  expense is saved with Ali as payer and Sara and Bilal as the only sharers.

**Invalid input:**
- Given the form, when I submit with no description, then the form shows
  "Description cannot be empty" and no expense is saved.
- Given the form, when I enter amount 0, then the form shows "Amount must be
  greater than zero".
- Given the form, when I enter a negative amount (e.g. −500), then the form
  shows "Amount must be greater than zero".
- Given the form, when I enter 999.50, then the form shows "Amount must be a
  whole number of rupees".
- Given the form, when I select zero sharers, then the form shows "At least
  one participant must share this expense".
- Given the form, when I submit without selecting a payer, then the form shows
  "A payer must be selected".

**Boundary values:**
- Given the form, when I enter 1 (minimum valid amount), then the expense is
  saved.
- Given the form, when I enter Rs. 10,000,000, then the expense is saved.
- Given the form, when I enter Rs. 10,000,001, then the form shows "Amount
  cannot exceed Rs. 10,000,000".

**Large numbers:**
- Given Rs. 10,000,000 shared equally among 3 participants; when saved; then
  all shares display as whole-rupee figures and no value is shown in scientific
  notation.

**Continuation after error:**
- Given the form shows a validation error, when I correct all fields and
  resubmit, then the expense is saved and the error clears.

*(How shares are divided into whole rupees: see S-12. S-4 applies that rule;
it is not repeated here.)*

---

## S-5 — Add a tip to an expense
**Serves:** J-1, J-2 | **Status:** Not implemented

As a Trip Treasurer, I want to attach a tip to an expense as a whole
percentage or a flat rupee amount, so that the full amount actually paid is
included in each participant's share.

**Normal cases:**
- Given "Dinner" Rs. 1,000, tip 10%, shared equally by Ali and Sara; when
  saved; then total is Rs. 1,100 and each share is Rs. 550.
- Given "Dinner" Rs. 1,000, flat tip Rs. 100, shared equally by Ali and Sara;
  when saved; then total is Rs. 1,100 and each share is Rs. 550.
- Given "Fuel" Rs. 800, tip field left blank; when saved; then total is
  Rs. 800 (no tip applied).
- Given "Lunch" Rs. 600, tip 10%, shared by Ali and Sara but not Bilal; when
  saved; then total is Rs. 660, Ali Rs. 330, Sara Rs. 330, and Bilal owes
  nothing for this expense. *(Fairness: tip follows the sharers, not the
  whole group.)*

**Percentage tip rounding:**
- Given "Dinner" Rs. 1,235, tip 10%; the computed tip is Rs. 123.5, which
  rounds up to Rs. 124 (halves round up); total is Rs. 1,359.
- Given "Dinner" Rs. 1,234, tip 10%; the computed tip is Rs. 123.4, which
  rounds down to Rs. 123; total is Rs. 1,357.

**Invalid input:**
- Given the form, when I enter a flat tip of −50, then the form shows "Tip
  cannot be negative".
- Given the form, when I enter −10%, then the form shows "Tip cannot be
  negative".
- Given the form, when I enter 101%, then the form shows "Tip percentage
  cannot exceed 100%".
- Given the form, when I enter a flat tip of 99.50, then the form shows "Tip
  must be a whole number of rupees".

**Boundary values:**
- Given Rs. 500, tip exactly 100%; when saved; total is Rs. 1,000 and the
  expense is accepted.
- Given Rs. 500, tip 0%; when saved; total is Rs. 500.

**Tip causes total to exceed cap:**
- Given base Rs. 9,500,000 and flat tip Rs. 600,000 (total Rs. 10,100,000);
  then the form shows "Total including tip cannot exceed Rs. 10,000,000".
- Given base Rs. 9,500,000 and flat tip Rs. 500,000 (total Rs. 10,000,000);
  then the expense is saved.

*(Rounding when the tipped total is not evenly divisible: see S-12.)*

---

## S-6 — Edit an expense
**Serves:** J-1, J-2 | **Status:** Not implemented

As a Trip Treasurer, I want to edit a saved expense, so that I can correct
amounts, payers or participant lists after initial entry.

- Given expense "Fuel" Rs. 600; when I change the amount to Rs. 700 and save;
  then the expense shows Rs. 700.
- Given expense "Hotel" shared by Ali and Sara; when I change the sharers to
  Ali, Sara, and Bilal; then the expense shows three sharers.
- Given expense "Fuel" with payer Ali; when I change the payer to Sara; then
  the expense shows Sara as payer.
- Given the edit form; when I submit invalid input (zero amount, decimal,
  above cap, no sharers, invalid tip); then the same error messages as in S-4
  and S-5 apply and the original expense data is preserved.
- Given the settlement summary is displayed; when I save an edit; then the
  settlement recalculates automatically.

---

## S-7 — Delete an expense
**Serves:** J-1 | **Status:** Not implemented

As a Trip Treasurer, I want to delete an expense, so that I can remove entries
added by mistake.

- Given expense "Snacks" Rs. 200; when I choose to delete it and confirm; then
  "Snacks" no longer appears in the expense list.
- Given I tap delete on an expense; then the app prompts for confirmation
  before removing it — a single accidental tap does not delete the expense.
- Given I tap delete and then cancel at the confirmation prompt; then the
  expense remains unchanged.
- Given the settlement summary is displayed and I delete an expense and
  confirm; then the settlement recalculates automatically.

---

## S-8 — Persist trip data in the browser
**Serves:** J-1 | **Status:** Not implemented

As a Trip Treasurer, I want the trip data to save automatically in my browser,
so that I can close the tab or restart the browser at any point during a
multi-day trip without losing any entered data.

- Given I have added participants Ali, Sara and expense "Fuel" Rs. 600; when I
  close the tab and reopen the app in the same browser on the same device;
  then Ali, Sara and "Fuel" Rs. 600 are still present.
- Given I have entered trip data; when I restart the browser and reopen the
  app; then all participants and expenses are restored exactly as entered.
- Given I add or edit an expense; then the change is saved immediately — no
  manual "save trip" action is required.
- Given the app is opened for the first time (no data in localStorage); then
  the app starts with an empty trip and shows no error or message.
- Given localStorage contains data for this app that cannot be parsed (e.g.
  the storage was corrupted); then the app shows "Your saved trip data could
  not be loaded. Starting a new trip." and starts with an empty trip rather
  than crashing or silently discarding the data.

---

## S-9 — Start a new trip
**Serves:** J-1 | **Status:** Not implemented

As a Trip Treasurer, I want to clear all current trip data and start fresh,
so that I can use the app for a new trip without previous data interfering.

- Given the trip has participants and expenses; when I choose "Start new trip"
  and confirm; then the participant list and expense list are both empty and
  localStorage is cleared.
- Given I choose "Start new trip"; when I cancel at the confirmation prompt;
  then all participants and expenses remain intact.
- Given the trip is already empty; when I choose "Start new trip" and confirm;
  then the app remains on an empty state with no error.

---

## S-10 — View the settlement summary
**Serves:** J-3 | **Status:** Not implemented

As a Trip Treasurer, I want to see a labelled list of transfers that clears
all balances, so that the group knows exactly who pays whom and the trip is
fully settled.

**Normal cases:**
- Given Ali paid Rs. 600 for "Fuel" shared equally by Ali and Sara (each
  Rs. 300); then the settlement shows "Sara pays Ali Rs. 300".
- Given the Faisalabad scenario:
  - "Fuel to Faisalabad" Rs. 1,500, paid by Ali, shared by Ali and Usman
    (Rs. 750 each, no rounding)
  - "Fuel onwards" Rs. 2,000, paid by Usman, shared by Ali, Usman, Sara,
    Bilal (Rs. 500 each, no rounding)
  - "Hotel" Rs. 3,001, paid by Sara, shared by Ali, Usman, Sara, Bilal
    (Sara is payer and sharer — Sara Rs. 751, others Rs. 750 each per S-12)

  Net balances: Ali −Rs. 500, Usman Rs. 0, Sara +Rs. 1,750,
  Bilal −Rs. 1,250.

  Then the settlement shows: "Bilal pays Sara Rs. 1,250" and
  "Ali pays Sara Rs. 500".

- Given all net balances are zero; then the settlement shows "All balances
  are settled — no transfers needed."
- Given only one participant exists; then the settlement shows "All balances
  are settled — no transfers needed."

**Empty state:**
- Given no expenses have been added; when I view the settlement; then the app
  shows "No expenses have been added yet."

**Algorithm label:**
- The settlement section is headed "Simplified settlement" (not "Minimum
  transfers") to reflect that the greedy algorithm is not guaranteed to be
  the mathematical minimum.

**Mathematical invariant (verified by automated tests):**
- Given any set of valid expenses; when the settlement is computed; then
  applying all listed transfers to participants' net balances brings every
  balance to exactly Rs. 0.

**Continuation:**
- Given the settlement is displayed; when I add, edit or delete an expense;
  then the settlement recalculates automatically.

---

## S-11 — View the per-person breakdown
**Serves:** J-2, J-4 | **Status:** Not implemented

As a Trip Treasurer, I want to see a breakdown for each participant showing
the expenses they shared, their share of each, what they personally paid, and
their net balance, so that any group member can verify their own figure without
argument.

**Normal cases:**
- Given Ali paid Rs. 600 for "Fuel" (shared Ali, Sara — each Rs. 300), and
  Sara paid Rs. 900 for "Hotel" (shared Ali, Sara, Bilal — each Rs. 300);
  Ali's breakdown shows:
  - "Fuel": share Rs. 300, paid Rs. 600 → net from this expense: +Rs. 300
  - "Hotel": share Rs. 300, paid Rs. 0 → net from this expense: −Rs. 300
  - Summary: total paid Rs. 600, total owed Rs. 600, net balance Rs. 0
- Given Bilal was not on "Fuel"; then "Fuel" does not appear in Bilal's
  breakdown.
- Given Ali paid Rs. 300 for "Snacks" shared by Sara and Bilal only (Ali is
  payer but not a sharer); Ali's breakdown shows "Snacks": paid Rs. 300,
  share Rs. 0, net from this expense +Rs. 300.

**Consistency with settlement:**
- Given both the per-person breakdown and the settlement summary are
  displayed; then each participant's net balance in the breakdown matches
  exactly the net balance used in the settlement calculation.

**Zero balance:**
- Given a participant's total paid equals their total owed; then their
  breakdown shows net balance Rs. 0 and they do not appear in the settlement
  transfers.

*(Share values in the breakdown use the same rounded whole-rupee figures
defined in S-12.)*

---

## S-12 — See how each expense's shares were rounded
**Serves:** J-2, J-4 | **Status:** Not implemented

As a Trip Treasurer, I want to see, for each expense, how the total was
divided into whole-rupee shares and who absorbed the leftover, so that any
participant can confirm the rounding was consistent and fair.

### Canonical rounding rule
*(Referenced by S-4, S-5, S-10, S-11 — defined once here.)*

For an expense with total T (base + any rounded tip), payer P, and n sharers
listed in a fixed order:

**Case A — P is one of the n sharers:**
1. Every sharer except P receives ⌊T ÷ n⌋.
2. P receives T − (n − 1) × ⌊T ÷ n⌋. P absorbs the leftover.
3. Invariant: all n shares sum to T exactly.

**Case B — P is not one of the n sharers:**
1. Base share for each sharer: ⌊T ÷ n⌋.
2. Leftover = T − n × ⌊T ÷ n⌋ (between 0 and n − 1 rupees).
3. The first `leftover` sharers in listed order each receive one extra rupee.
4. Invariant: all n shares sum to T exactly.

**Tip rounding:** when a percentage tip is entered, the computed rupee amount
is rounded to the nearest whole rupee before being added to the base (halves
round up). The rounded total T is then divided as above.

**Shares always sum exactly to T in both cases.**

### Acceptance criteria

**Case A — payer is a sharer:**
- Given Rs. 1,000, paid by Ali, shared by Ali → Sara → Bilal (listed order):
  Sara Rs. 333, Bilal Rs. 333, Ali Rs. 334 (absorbs Re. 1). Display shows
  "Ali absorbed Re. 1 rounding difference."
- Given Rs. 900, paid by Ali, shared by Ali → Sara → Bilal: each Rs. 300, no
  remainder. Display shows "No rounding needed."
- Given Rs. 1,001, paid by Ali, shared by Ali → Sara → Bilal: Sara Rs. 333,
  Bilal Rs. 333, Ali Rs. 335 (absorbs Rs. 2). Display shows "Ali absorbed
  Rs. 2 rounding difference."

**Case B — payer is not a sharer:**
- Given Rs. 1,000, paid by Ali (not sharing), shared by Sara → Bilal →
  Kamran: ⌊1000 ÷ 3⌋ = 333, leftover = 1. Sara Rs. 334, Bilal Rs. 333,
  Kamran Rs. 333. Sum = 1,000. Display shows "Re. 1 rounding difference added
  to Sara's share (first in listed order)."
- Given Rs. 1,001, paid by Ali (not sharing), shared by Sara → Bilal →
  Kamran: leftover = 2. Sara Rs. 334, Bilal Rs. 334, Kamran Rs. 333.
  Sum = 1,001. Display shows "Rs. 2 rounding difference distributed to Sara
  and Bilal (first in listed order)."
- Given Rs. 1,000, paid by Ali (not sharing), shared by Sara → Bilal only
  (2 sharers): 1000 ÷ 2 = 500 exactly. Sara Rs. 500, Bilal Rs. 500. No
  rounding note shown.

**Very small amounts:**
- Given Rs. 2, paid by Ali (not sharing), shared by Sara → Bilal → Kamran:
  ⌊2 ÷ 3⌋ = 0, leftover = 2. Sara Rs. 1, Bilal Rs. 1, Kamran Rs. 0.
  Sum = 2. Display shows "Rs. 2 rounding difference distributed to Sara and
  Bilal (first in listed order)." Kamran's share is Rs. 0 and still appears
  in the breakdown.

**With tip (Case A):**
- Given Rs. 1,000 + 10% tip = Rs. 1,100 total, paid by Ali (payer and
  sharer), shared by Ali → Sara → Bilal: ⌊1100 ÷ 3⌋ = 366, leftover = 2.
  Sara Rs. 366, Bilal Rs. 366, Ali Rs. 368. Display shows "Ali absorbed
  Rs. 2 rounding difference."

**Consistency:**
- The shares shown in S-12 are identical to those used in S-11 (per-person
  breakdown) and S-10 (settlement). There is one source of truth for rounding.

---

## "They must never" coverage

| Constraint from app-roles.md | Covered by |
|---|---|
| See a settlement where transfers do not account for every rupee of every net balance | S-10: mathematical invariant criterion |
| See shares on an expense that do not sum to the expense total including tip | S-12: invariant — shares sum exactly to T in both Case A and Case B |
| Lose entered data without an explicit confirmation step | S-7: delete confirmation; S-9: new-trip confirmation; S-8: corrupt-data message instead of silent discard |
| Remove a participant who is named on one or more expenses — app blocks and names the expenses | S-3: blocked-as-sharer, blocked-as-payer, multi-expense message |
| Submit an expense with no participants sharing it | S-4: "At least one participant must share this expense" |
| Enter a zero or negative expense amount | S-4: "Amount must be greater than zero" |
| Add a participant with an empty or duplicate name | S-1: empty-name and duplicate criteria; S-2: same on rename |
| Enter an amount that is not a whole number of rupees | S-4: "Amount must be a whole number of rupees"; S-5: "Tip must be a whole number of rupees" |
| Enter a single expense amount above Rs. 10,000,000 | S-4: boundary criteria; S-5: total-including-tip cap |
| Enter a negative tip, or a percentage tip above 100% | S-5: negative-tip and >100% criteria |

content.thinking:
Let me carefully review the user stories for anything ambiguous, contradictory, or untestable, then propose a build plan.

**Spec issues to flag:**

1. **S-12 display text for rounding: Re. 1 vs Rs. 1** — the stories use "Re. 1" (singular rupee) vs "Rs. 2" etc. This is linguistically correct (Re. = singular rupee in Pakistani/Indian convention) but needs to be consistent in implementation. Not a contradiction but worth noting.

2. **S-12, very small amounts: Kamran's share is Rs. 0** — the spec says "Kamran's share is Rs. 0 and still appears in the breakdown." This confirms zero-share sharers still get listed, which is consistent and testable.

3. I also notice Case A and Case B use different rounding-note wording — "Ali absorbed Re. 1 rounding difference" versus "Re. 1 rounding difference added to Sara's share" — so I need to reproduce each display string exactly as written rather than treating them as interchangeable.

4. Now I want to verify the math behind the S-10 Faisalabad fuel scenario.

I'm checking the Faisalabad "Fuel to" split of Rs. 1,500 paid by Ali and shared with Usman: dividing 1500/2 gives 750 each, confirming the figures. Then the "Fuel onwards" Rs. 2,000 paid by Usman split across four people gives 500 each, which also checks out. Now I'm verifying the Hotel bill of Rs. 3,001 paid by Sara and split among four people under Case A.

Dividing 3001 by 4 gives 750 for each of the others, with Sara absorbing the remainder to get 751, matching the expected spec exactly. I'm now computing net balances for each person by comparing what they paid against what they owed across all three expenses -- Ali nets -500, Usman nets 0, and I'm starting to tally Sara's net balance from her payments and owed shares.

Sara nets +1,750 and Bilal nets -1,250, which sets up the settlement calculation. Using greedy matching, Bilal pays Sara 1,250 and Ali pays Sara 500, exactly resolving all balances -- confirming the settlement instructions should read "Bilal pays Sara Rs. 1,250" and "Ali pays Sara Rs. 500." Now I'm moving to check the grammar of the S-3 blocking message.

I need to track the difference between plural "they appear on Fuel and Hotel" versus singular "that expense" phrasing, since this depends on how many expenses are affected -- a detail requiring careful code handling. I'm also noticing that S-12's rounding note text differs by case: Case A with an exact split (900/3) shows "No rounding needed," while Case B's even two-way split shows "No rounding note shown" instead -- these are distinct strings tied to different scenarios that need separate verification.

For the duplicate name check, the comparison is case-insensitive but displayed names likely preserve the user's original typed case since the spec doesn't clarify storage format.

Looking at S-2, renaming "Ali" to "Ali" with no actual change is accepted, meaning the duplicate check must exclude the person currently being renamed. But this raises a question: if someone renames "Ali" to "ali" — just a case change — does that count as "same name" and get allowed, or is it treated as a new duplicate check against itself? The spec doesn't test this edge case directly, so I'll need to flag it for clarification.

For S-11's per-expense net calculation, when Ali pays but doesn't share in an expense, the net is simply paid minus share, which checks out fine.

Another unclear point is where S-12's rounding information actually gets displayed — whether in the expense list, the per-person breakdown, or some other UI element — since the spec just says "display shows" without specifying location.

Also worth noting: S-4 requires the payer field to start unselected rather than defaulting to the first participant, so the "must select a payer" validation actually triggers.

Now I'm sketching the architecture: a logic layer separating types, validation, rounding, tip calculation, balance computation, and settlement algorithm from a UI layer with app state and components, plus a storage module for localStorage persistence. I'm planning to build the pure logic first, testable without any DOM dependency, before wiring up the UI.

Continuing the UI phase plan: edit/delete expense, auto-persistence wiring, new trip button, settlement summary, per-person breakdown, and rounding notes display. I also note the commands for install, dev, test, and build, and I'm starting to flag spec issues — first up, the inconsistency in S-12 around how "no rounding needed" is displayed between Case A and Case B.

I'm continuing the spec issue list: S-12 lacks clarity on where rounding notes appear in the UI, the singular/plural rupee phrasing just needs careful implementation rather than clarification, S-3's error message wording for single vs multiple expenses is already spelled out, and there's a question about whether S-11's per-person breakdown should also surface the rounding note described in S-12.

Looking closer at S-12's title about seeing how each expense's shares were rounded, I think the rounding note naturally belongs to the expense entry or a per-expense detail view, while S-11's breakdown table likely only shows the share figures without repeating that note, since S-11 itself never mentions rounding. I'm ready to put together my answer now.

## Step 1: Spec review — issues to resolve before coding

### 1. S-12 — rounding note wording is inconsistent between Case A and Case B when no rounding occurs
- Case A, Rs. 900 ÷ 3 (exact): **Display shows "No rounding needed."** (affirmative note)
- Case B, Rs. 1,000 ÷ 2 (exact): **"No rounding note shown."** (silence)

These are two different behaviours for the same situation (zero leftover). I need a decision: does Case A always show a note, or do both cases suppress the note when leftover = 0?

My suggestion: suppress the note in both cases when leftover = 0. If you prefer "No rounding needed." shown for Case A only, I can implement that — but please confirm.

### 2. S-12 — UI placement of rounding notes is unspecified
The story says "Display shows…" but never says *where*. Options:
- As a note beneath each expense in the expense list
- Only inside a per-expense detail/expand view
- Also echoed in the per-person breakdown (S-11)?

S-11 explicitly says shares use the "same rounded whole-rupee figures defined in S-12" but is silent on showing the note there. I propose: rounding note appears as a collapsible/visible line under each expense in the main expense list, and is **not** repeated in the per-person breakdown (S-11 shows numbers only). Confirm or redirect.

### 3. S-2 — renaming to a differently-cased version of the same name
Spec says renaming "Ali" to "Ali" (no change) is accepted. The duplicate check is case-insensitive. If I rename "Ali" to "ali", the case-insensitive duplicate check would match "Ali" — but "Ali" is the same person being renamed, so it should be allowed. The spec doesn't test this edge case explicitly. My implementation will: skip the duplicate check when the new name equals the old name (case-insensitively). Flag if you want a different rule.

### 4. No issues
S-10 Faisalabad numbers check out exactly (I verified all arithmetic). S-3 singular/plural ("that expense" vs "those expenses") is specified correctly. S-5 tip rounding ("halves round up") is consistent with standard Rs. rounding.

---

## Step 2: Build plan

### Reviewer commands
```
npm install          # install deps (Node 20 required)
npm run dev          # starts Vite dev server → open http://localhost:5173
npm test             # runs Vitest unit suite (watch-off: npm test -- --run)
npm run build        # optional production build
```

### Project setup
- **Vite** + **vanilla TypeScript** (no framework)
- **Vitest** for unit tests
- `tsconfig` targeting ES2020, `strict: true`
- No backend, no external dependencies beyond Vite and Vitest

### Architecture
```
src/
  logic/
    types.ts         ← Participant, Expense, TipInput, Share, NetBalance, Transfer
    validation.ts    ← all error message functions (S-1–S-5 rules)
    rounding.ts      ← computeShares(T, payerId, sharers[]) → Share[]  (S-12)
    tip.ts           ← computeTip(base, tipInput) → { tipAmount, total }  (S-5)
    balances.ts      ← computeNetBalances(expenses) → NetBalance[]  (S-10, S-11)
    settlement.ts    ← computeSettlement(balances) → Transfer[]  (S-10)
    storage.ts       ← loadTrip() / saveTrip()  (S-8)
  ui/
    state.ts         ← single mutable AppState + update/render cycle
    participants.ts  ← participant panel (S-1, S-2, S-3)
    expenseForm.ts   ← add/edit form (S-4, S-5, S-6)
    expenseList.ts   ← list with delete + rounding notes (S-7, S-12)
    settlement.ts    ← settlement view (S-10)
    breakdown.ts     ← per-person breakdown (S-11)
    newTrip.ts       ← new trip button + confirm (S-9)
  main.ts            ← wires storage + renders on load (S-8)
index.html
```

**Key principle:** every function in `src/logic/` takes plain data in, returns plain data out — zero DOM, zero side effects, fully deterministic. UI files are the only thing that touches the DOM or localStorage.

### Build order and rationale

**Wave 1 — logic layer (no UI yet, all tested)**

| Order | Module | Stories covered |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `types.ts` | foundation for everything |
| 2 | `validation.ts` | S-1, S-2, S-3, S-4, S-5 error messages |
| 3 | `tip.ts` | S-5 tip + percentage rounding |
| 4 | `rounding.ts` | S-12 computeShares (Case A & B) |
| 5 | `balances.ts` | S-10, S-11 net balance formula |
| 6 | `settlement.ts` | S-10 greedy algorithm + invariant |
| 7 | `storage.ts` | S-8 load/save + corrupt-data handling |

All logic has unit tests before any UI is written. Every numeric example in the stories becomes a named test case.

**Wave 2 — UI, story by story**

| Order | Stories | Why this order |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | S-1, S-2, S-3 | Participants must exist before expenses can reference them |
| 2 | S-4, S-5 | Core data entry; tip is part of the add form |
| 3 | S-6, S-7 | Edit/delete complete the CRUD cycle |
| 4 | S-8 | Wire auto-save + load; needs expenses to exist to verify |
| 5 | S-9 | New trip; needs data to clear |
| 6 | S-10 | Settlement view; needs full expense data |
| 7 | S-11 | Per-person breakdown; shares already computed for S-10 |
| 8 | S-12 | Rounding notes; last because display placement depends on your answer above |

### Test naming convention
```
// rounding.test.ts
describe("S-12 computeShares", () => {
  it("S-12 Case A: Rs. 1000 / 3, payer absorbs Re. 1")
  it("S-12 Case A: Rs. 900 / 3 exact, no remainder")
  it("S-12 Case A: Rs. 1001 / 3, payer absorbs Rs. 2")
  it("S-12 Case B: Rs. 1000, payer not sharing, leftover to first sharer")
  it("S-12 Case B: Rs. 1001, leftover 2, distributed to first two sharers")
  it("S-12 very small: Rs. 2 / 3, Kamran gets Rs. 0")
  it("S-12 with tip: Rs. 1000 + 10% = Rs. 1100 / 3, Case A")
  // etc.
})

describe("S-10 computeSettlement", () => {
  it("S-10: Faisalabad scenario — Bilal pays Sara 1250, Ali pays Sara 500")
  it("S-10: all balances zero → no transfers")
  it("S-10: mathematical invariant — transfers zero out all balances")
})
```

---

**Two open questions I need answers to before I write any code:**

1. **S-12 rounding note, zero-remainder case**: suppress in both Case A and Case B (my suggestion), or show "No rounding needed." for Case A only?
2. **S-12 rounding note placement**: note under each expense in the expense list (not in per-person breakdown)?

Once you confirm these two points (and correct anything in the build plan you disagree with), I'll start Wave 1.

  and requires no separate role.

  multiple payers produce a genuinely hard calculation problem that phone
  calculators and mental arithmetic fail at. The Faisalabad trip scenario

# User Stories

*All stories have status: Not implemented. Statuses are updated after each
story is built and verified against its acceptance criteria.*

---

## S-1 — Add a participant
**Serves:** J-1 | **Status:** Not implemented

As a Trip Treasurer, I want to add a named participant to the trip, so that
they can be assigned as payers or included in expense splits.

- Given an empty roster, when I type "Ali" and confirm, then "Ali" appears
  in the participant list.
- Given "Ali" is already in the roster, when I add "Sara", then both appear
  in the list.
- Given the add-participant form, when I submit an empty name (or a name of
  only spaces), then the form shows "Name cannot be empty" and no participant
  is added.
- Given "Ali" is in the roster, when I try to add "Ali" (same name,
  case-insensitive), then the form shows "A participant named Ali already
  exists" and no duplicate is added.
- Given the form shows an error, when I enter a valid unique name and confirm,
  then the participant is added and the error clears.

---

## S-2 — Rename a participant
**Serves:** J-1 | **Status:** Not implemented

As a Trip Treasurer, I want to rename a participant, so that I can correct a
typo or name change without losing their expense data.

- Given "Ali" is in the roster, when I rename them to "Ali Khan" and confirm,
  then "Ali Khan" appears in the list and all expenses that referenced "Ali"
  now reference "Ali Khan".

  expense is accepted.
- Given Rs. 500, tip 0%; when saved; total is Rs. 500.

**Tip causes total to exceed cap:**
- Given base Rs. 9,500,000 and flat tip Rs. 600,000 (total Rs. 10,100,000);
  then the form shows "Total including tip cannot exceed Rs. 10,000,000".
- Given base Rs. 9,500,000 and flat tip Rs. 500,000 (total Rs. 10,000,000);

## S-10 — View the settlement summary
**Serves:** J-3 | **Status:** Not implemented

As a Trip Treasurer, I want to see a labelled list of transfers that clears
all balances, so that the group knows exactly who pays whom and the trip is
fully settled.

**Normal cases:**
- Given Ali paid Rs. 600 for "Fuel" shared equally by Ali and Sara (each
  Rs. 300); then the settlement shows "Sara pays Ali Rs. 300".
- Given the Faisalabad scenario:
  - "Fuel to Faisalabad" Rs. 1,500, paid by Ali, shared by Ali and Usman
    (Rs. 750 each, no rounding)
  - "Fuel onwards" Rs. 2,000, paid by Usman, shared by Ali, Usman, Sara,
    Bilal (Rs. 500 each, no rounding)
  - "Hotel" Rs. 3,001, paid by Sara, shared by Ali, Usman, Sara, Bilal
    (Sara is payer and sharer — Sara Rs. 751, others Rs. 750 each per S-12)

  Net balances: Ali −Rs. 500, Usman Rs. 0, Sara +Rs. 1,750,
  Bilal −Rs. 1,250.

  Then the settlement shows: "Bilal pays Sara Rs. 1,250" and
  "Ali pays Sara Rs. 500".

- Given all net balances are zero; then the settlement shows "All balances
  are settled — no transfers needed."
- Given only one participant exists; then the settlement shows "All balances
  are settled — no transfers needed."

**Empty state:**
- Given no expenses have been added; when I view the settlement; then the app
  shows "No expenses have been added yet."

**Algorithm label:**
- The settlement section is headed "Simplified settlement" (not "Minimum
  transfers") to reflect that the greedy algorithm is not guaranteed to be
  the mathematical minimum.

**Mathematical invariant (verified by automated tests):**
- Given any set of valid expenses; when the settlement is computed; then
  applying all listed transfers to participants' net balances brings every
  balance to exactly Rs. 0.

**Continuation:**
- Given the settlement is displayed; when I add, edit or delete an expense;
  then the settlement recalculates automatically.

## S-11 — View the per-person breakdown
**Serves:** J-2, J-4 | **Status:** Not implemented

As a Trip Treasurer, I want to see a breakdown for each participant showing

their net balance, so that any group member can verify their own figure without

**Normal cases:**
- Given Ali paid Rs. 600 for "Fuel" (shared Ali, Sara — each Rs. 300), and
  Sara paid Rs. 900 for "Hotel" (shared Ali, Sara, Bilal — each Rs. 300);
  Ali's breakdown shows:

  - "Hotel": share Rs. 300, paid Rs. 0 → net from this expense: −Rs. 300
  - Summary: total paid Rs. 600, total owed Rs. 600, net balance Rs. 0
- Given Bilal was not on "Fuel"; then "Fuel" does not appear in Bilal's
  breakdown.
- Given Ali paid Rs. 300 for "Snacks" shared by Sara and Bilal only (Ali is
  payer but not a sharer); Ali's breakdown shows "Snacks": paid Rs. 300,
  share Rs. 0, net from this expense +Rs. 300.

**Consistency with settlement:**
- Given both the per-person breakdown and the settlement summary are
  displayed; then each participant's net balance in the breakdown matches
  exactly the net balance used in the settlement calculation.

**Zero balance:**
- Given a participant's total paid equals their total owed; then their
  breakdown shows net balance Rs. 0 and they do not appear in the settlement

defined in S-12.)*

## S-12 — See how each expense's shares were rounded
**Serves:** J-2, J-4 | **Status:** Not implemented

As a Trip Treasurer, I want to see, for each expense, how the total was
divided into whole-rupee shares and who absorbed the leftover, so that any
participant can confirm the rounding was consistent and fair.

### Canonical rounding rule
*(Referenced by S-4, S-5, S-10, S-11 — defined once here.)*

For an expense with total T (base + any rounded tip), payer P, and n sharers
listed in a fixed order:

**Case A — P is one of the n sharers:**
1. Every sharer except P receives ⌊T ÷ n⌋.
2. P receives T − (n − 1) × ⌊T ÷ n⌋. P absorbs the leftover.
3. Invariant: all n shares sum to T exactly.

**Case B — P is not one of the n sharers:**
1. Base share for each sharer: ⌊T ÷ n⌋.
2. Leftover = T − n × ⌊T ÷ n⌋ (between 0 and n − 1 rupees).
3. The first `leftover` sharers in listed order each receive one extra rupee.
4. Invariant: all n shares sum to T exactly.

**Tip rounding:** when a percentage tip is entered, the computed rupee amount
is rounded to the nearest whole rupee before being added to the base (halves
round up). The rounded total T is then divided as above.

**Shares always sum exactly to T in both cases.**

### Acceptance criteria

**Case A — payer is a sharer:**
- Given Rs. 1,000, paid by Ali, shared by Ali → Sara → Bilal (listed order):
  Sara Rs. 333, Bilal Rs. 333, Ali Rs. 334 (absorbs Re. 1). Display shows
  "Ali absorbed Re. 1 rounding difference."
- Given Rs. 900, paid by Ali, shared by Ali → Sara → Bilal: each Rs. 300, no
  remainder. Display shows "No rounding needed."
- Given Rs. 1,001, paid by Ali, shared by Ali → Sara → Bilal: Sara Rs. 333,
  Bilal Rs. 333, Ali Rs. 335 (absorbs Rs. 2). Display shows "Ali absorbed
  Rs. 2 rounding difference."

**Case B — payer is not a sharer:**
- Given Rs. 1,000, paid by Ali (not sharing), shared by Sara → Bilal →
  Kamran: ⌊1000 ÷ 3⌋ = 333, leftover = 1. Sara Rs. 334, Bilal Rs. 333,
  Kamran Rs. 333. Sum = 1,000. Display shows "Re. 1 rounding difference added
  to Sara's share (first in listed order)."
- Given Rs. 1,001, paid by Ali (not sharing), shared by Sara → Bilal →
  Kamran: leftover = 2. Sara Rs. 334, Bilal Rs. 334, Kamran Rs. 333.
  Sum = 1,001. Display shows "Rs. 2 rounding difference distributed to Sara
  and Bilal (first in listed order)."
- Given Rs. 1,000, paid by Ali (not sharing), shared by Sara → Bilal only
  (2 sharers): 1000 ÷ 2 = 500 exactly. Sara Rs. 500, Bilal Rs. 500. No
  rounding note shown.

**Very small amounts:**
- Given Rs. 2, paid by Ali (not sharing), shared by Sara → Bilal → Kamran:
  ⌊2 ÷ 3⌋ = 0, leftover = 2. Sara Rs. 1, Bilal Rs. 1, Kamran Rs. 0.
  Sum = 2. Display shows "Rs. 2 rounding difference distributed to Sara and
  Bilal (first in listed order)." Kamran's share is Rs. 0 and still appears
  in the breakdown.

**With tip (Case A):**
- Given Rs. 1,000 + 10% tip = Rs. 1,100 total, paid by Ali (payer and
  sharer), shared by Ali → Sara → Bilal: ⌊1100 ÷ 3⌋ = 366, leftover = 2.
  Sara Rs. 366, Bilal Rs. 366, Ali Rs. 368. Display shows "Ali absorbed
  Rs. 2 rounding difference."

**Consistency:**
- The shares shown in S-12 are identical to those used in S-11 (per-person
  breakdown) and S-10 (settlement). There is one source of truth for rounding.

---

## "They must never" coverage

| Constraint from app-roles.md | Covered by |
|---|---|
| See a settlement where transfers do not account for every rupee of every net balance | S-10: mathematical invariant criterion |
| See shares on an expense that do not sum to the expense total including tip | S-12: invariant — shares sum exactly to T in both Case A and Case B |
| Lose entered data without an explicit confirmation step | S-7: delete confirmation; S-9: new-trip confirmation; S-8: corrupt-data message instead of silent discard |
| Remove a participant who is named on one or more expenses — app blocks and names the expenses | S-3: blocked-as-sharer, blocked-as-payer, multi-expense message |
| Submit an expense with no participants sharing it | S-4: "At least one participant must share this expense" |
| Enter a zero or negative expense amount | S-4: "Amount must be greater than zero" |
| Add a participant with an empty or duplicate name | S-1: empty-name and duplicate criteria; S-2: same on rename |
| Enter an amount that is not a whole number of rupees | S-4: "Amount must be a whole number of rupees"; S-5: "Tip must be a whole number of rupees" |
| Enter a single expense amount above Rs. 10,000,000 | S-4: boundary criteria; S-5: total-including-tip cap |
| Enter a negative tip, or a percentage tip above 100% | S-5: negative-tip and >100% criteria |

# User Stories

*All stories have status: Not implemented. Statuses are updated after each
story is built and verified against its acceptance criteria.*

---

## S-1 — Add a participant
**Serves:** J-1 | **Status:** Not implemented

As a Trip Treasurer, I want to add a named participant to the trip, so that
they can be assigned as payers or included in expense splits.

- Given an empty roster, when I type "Ali" and confirm, then "Ali" appears
  in the participant list.
- Given "Ali" is already in the roster, when I add "Sara", then both appear
  in the list.
- Given the add-participant form, when I submit an empty name (or a name of
  only spaces), then the form shows "Name cannot be empty" and no participant
  is added.
- Given "Ali" is in the roster, when I try to add "Ali" (same name,
  case-insensitive), then the form shows "A participant named Ali already
  exists" and no duplicate is added.
- Given the form shows an error, when I enter a valid unique name and confirm,
  then the participant is added and the error clears.

---

## S-2 — Rename a participant
**Serves:** J-1 | **Status:** Not implemented

As a Trip Treasurer, I want to rename a participant, so that I can correct a
typo or name change without losing their expense data.

- Given "Ali" is in the roster, when I rename them to "Ali Khan" and confirm,
  then "Ali Khan" appears in the list and all expenses that referenced "Ali"
  now reference "Ali Khan".
- Given the rename form, when I submit an empty name, then the form shows
  "Name cannot be empty" and the name is unchanged.
- Given "Ali" and "Sara" are in the roster, when I rename "Ali" to "Sara",
  then the form shows "A participant named Sara already exists" and the name
  is unchanged.
- Given "Ali" is in the roster, when I rename "Ali" to "Ali" (no change),
  then the form is accepted without error.
- Given "Ali" is in the roster, when I rename "Ali" to "ali" (same name,
  different case), then the form is accepted without error and the
  participant's name is updated to "ali".
- Given the form shows an error, when I enter a valid unique name and confirm,
  then the rename succeeds and the error clears.

---

## S-3 — Remove a participant

## S-12 — See how each expense's shares were rounded
**Serves:** J-2, J-4 | **Status:** Not implemented

As a Trip Treasurer, I want to see, for each expense, how the total was
divided into whole-rupee shares and who absorbed the leftover, so that any
participant can confirm the rounding was consistent and fair.

### Canonical rounding rule
*(Referenced by S-4, S-5, S-10, S-11 — defined once here.)*

For an expense with total T (base + any rounded tip), payer P, and n sharers
listed in a fixed order:

**Case A — P is one of the n sharers:**
1. Every sharer except P receives ⌊T ÷ n⌋.
2. P receives T − (n − 1) × ⌊T ÷ n⌋. P absorbs the leftover.
3. Invariant: all n shares sum to T exactly.

**Case B — P is not one of the n sharers:**
1. Base share for each sharer: ⌊T ÷ n⌋.
2. Leftover = T − n × ⌊T ÷ n⌋ (between 0 and n − 1 rupees).
3. The first `leftover` sharers in listed order each receive one extra rupee.
4. Invariant: all n shares sum to T exactly.

**Tip rounding:** when a percentage tip is entered, the computed rupee amount
is rounded to the nearest whole rupee before being added to the base (halves
round up). The rounded total T is then divided as above.

**Shares always sum exactly to T in both cases.**

### Acceptance criteria

**Case A — payer is a sharer:**
- Given Rs. 1,000, paid by Ali, shared by Ali → Sara → Bilal (listed order):
  Sara Rs. 333, Bilal Rs. 333, Ali Rs. 334 (absorbs Re. 1). Display shows
  "Ali absorbed Re. 1 rounding difference."
- Given Rs. 900, paid by Ali, shared by Ali → Sara → Bilal: each Rs. 300, no
  remainder. Display shows "No rounding needed."
- Given Rs. 1,001, paid by Ali, shared by Ali → Sara → Bilal: Sara Rs. 333,
  Bilal Rs. 333, Ali Rs. 335 (absorbs Rs. 2). Display shows "Ali absorbed
  Rs. 2 rounding difference."

**Case B — payer is not a sharer:**
- Given Rs. 1,000, paid by Ali (not sharing), shared by Sara → Bilal →
  Kamran: ⌊1000 ÷ 3⌋ = 333, leftover = 1. Sara Rs. 334, Bilal Rs. 333,
  Kamran Rs. 333. Sum = 1,000. Display shows "Re. 1 rounding difference added
  to Sara's share (first in listed order)."
- Given Rs. 1,001, paid by Ali (not sharing), shared by Sara → Bilal →
  Kamran: leftover = 2. Sara Rs. 334, Bilal Rs. 334, Kamran Rs. 333.
  Sum = 1,001. Display shows "Rs. 2 rounding difference distributed to Sara
  and Bilal (first in listed order)."
- Given Rs. 1,000, paid by Ali (not sharing), shared by Sara → Bilal only
  (2 sharers): 1000 ÷ 2 = 500 exactly. Sara Rs. 500, Bilal Rs. 500. No
  rounding note shown.

**Very small amounts:**
- Given Rs. 2, paid by Ali (not sharing), shared by Sara → Bilal → Kamran:
  ⌊2 ÷ 3⌋ = 0, leftover = 2. Sara Rs. 1, Bilal Rs. 1, Kamran Rs. 0.
  Sum = 2. Display shows "Rs. 2 rounding difference distributed to Sara and
  Bilal (first in listed order)." Kamran's share is Rs. 0 and still appears
  in the breakdown.

**With tip (Case A):**
- Given Rs. 1,000 + 10% tip = Rs. 1,100 total, paid by Ali (payer and
  sharer), shared by Ali → Sara → Bilal: ⌊1100 ÷ 3⌋ = 366, leftover = 2.
  Sara Rs. 366, Bilal Rs. 366, Ali Rs. 368. Display shows "Ali absorbed
  Rs. 2 rounding difference."

**Consistency:**
- The shares shown in S-12 are identical to those used in S-11 (per-person
  breakdown) and S-10 (settlement). There is one source of truth for rounding.
