# User Stories

*All stories have status: Not implemented. Statuses are updated after each
story is built and verified against its acceptance criteria.*

---

## S-1 — Add a participant
**Serves:** J-1 | **Status:** Not implemented

As a Trip Treasurer, I want to add a named participant to the trip, so that
they can be assigned as payers or included in expense splits.

- Given an empty roster, when I type "Ali" and confirm, then "Ali" appears
  in the participant list.
- Given "Ali" is already in the roster, when I add "Sara", then both appear
  in the list.
- Given the add-participant form, when I submit an empty name (or a name of
  only spaces), then the form shows "Name cannot be empty" and no participant
  is added.
- Given "Ali" is in the roster, when I try to add "Ali" (same name,
  case-insensitive), then the form shows "A participant named Ali already
  exists" and no duplicate is added.
- Given the form shows an error, when I enter a valid unique name and confirm,
  then the participant is added and the error clears.

---

## S-2 — Rename a participant
**Serves:** J-1 | **Status:** Not implemented

As a Trip Treasurer, I want to rename a participant, so that I can correct a
typo or name change without losing their expense data.

- Given "Ali" is in the roster, when I rename them to "Ali Khan" and confirm,
  then "Ali Khan" appears in the list and all expenses that referenced "Ali"
  now reference "Ali Khan".
- Given the rename form, when I submit an empty name, then the form shows
  "Name cannot be empty" and the name is unchanged.
- Given "Ali" and "Sara" are in the roster, when I rename "Ali" to "Sara",
  then the form shows "A participant named Sara already exists" and the name
  is unchanged.
- Given "Ali" is in the roster, when I rename "Ali" to "Ali" (no change),
  then the form is accepted without error.
- Given "Ali" is in the roster, when I rename "Ali" to "ali" (same name,
  different case), then the form is accepted without error and the
  participant's name is updated to "ali".
- Given the form shows an error, when I enter a valid unique name and confirm,
  then the rename succeeds and the error clears.

---

## S-3 — Remove a participant
**Serves:** J-1 | **Status:** Not implemented

As a Trip Treasurer, I want to remove a participant from the trip, so that I
can correct mistakes in the group setup.

- Given "Ali" is in the roster and not named on any expense (neither as payer
  nor sharer), when I remove "Ali", then "Ali" no longer appears in the
  participant list.
- Given "Ali" is a sharer on "Fuel to Faisalabad", when I try to remove
  "Ali", then the app shows "Cannot remove Ali: they appear on Fuel to
  Faisalabad. Update that expense first." and Ali remains in the roster.
- Given "Ali" is the payer on "Snacks" but not a sharer on that expense, when
  I try to remove "Ali", then the app shows "Cannot remove Ali: they appear on
  Snacks. Update that expense first." and Ali remains.
- Given "Ali" appears on both "Fuel" and "Hotel", when I try to remove "Ali",
  then the message lists both: "Cannot remove Ali: they appear on Fuel and
  Hotel. Update those expenses first."
- Given Ali has been removed from all expenses they were named on, when I
  remove "Ali", then the removal succeeds.

---

## S-4 — Add an expense
**Serves:** J-1, J-2 | **Status:** Not implemented

As a Trip Treasurer, I want to add an expense with a description, total
amount, payer, and the subset of participants sharing it, so that I can record
exactly what was spent, who paid, and which members the cost applies to.

**Normal cases:**
- Given participants Ali, Sara, Bilal; when I save "Fuel" Rs. 900, paid by
  Ali, shared by Ali and Sara; then the expense shows description "Fuel",
  amount Rs. 900, payer Ali, sharers Ali and Sara.
- Given participants Ali, Sara, Bilal; when I save "Snacks" Rs. 300, paid by
  Ali, shared by Sara and Bilal (Ali is payer but not a sharer); then the
  expense is saved with Ali as payer and Sara and Bilal as the only sharers.

**Invalid input:**
- Given the form, when I submit with no description, then the form shows
  "Description cannot be empty" and no expense is saved.
- Given the form, when I enter amount 0, then the form shows "Amount must be
  greater than zero".
- Given the form, when I enter a negative amount (e.g. −500), then the form
  shows "Amount must be greater than zero".
- Given the form, when I enter 999.50, then the form shows "Amount must be a
  whole number of rupees".
- Given the form, when I select zero sharers, then the form shows "At least
  one participant must share this expense".
- Given the form, when I submit without selecting a payer, then the form shows
  "A payer must be selected".

**Boundary values:**
- Given the form, when I enter 1 (minimum valid amount), then the expense is
  saved.
- Given the form, when I enter Rs. 10,000,000, then the expense is saved.
- Given the form, when I enter Rs. 10,000,001, then the form shows "Amount
  cannot exceed Rs. 10,000,000".

**Large numbers:**
- Given Rs. 10,000,000 shared equally among 3 participants; when saved; then
  all shares display as whole-rupee figures and no value is shown in scientific
  notation.

**Continuation after error:**
- Given the form shows a validation error, when I correct all fields and
  resubmit, then the expense is saved and the error clears.

*(How shares are divided into whole rupees: see S-12. S-4 applies that rule;
it is not repeated here.)*

---

## S-5 — Add a tip to an expense
**Serves:** J-1, J-2 | **Status:** Not implemented

As a Trip Treasurer, I want to attach a tip to an expense as a whole
percentage or a flat rupee amount, so that the full amount actually paid is
included in each participant's share.

**Normal cases:**
- Given "Dinner" Rs. 1,000, tip 10%, shared equally by Ali and Sara; when
  saved; then total is Rs. 1,100 and each share is Rs. 550.
- Given "Dinner" Rs. 1,000, flat tip Rs. 100, shared equally by Ali and Sara;
  when saved; then total is Rs. 1,100 and each share is Rs. 550.
- Given "Fuel" Rs. 800, tip field left blank; when saved; then total is
  Rs. 800 (no tip applied).
- Given "Lunch" Rs. 600, tip 10%, shared by Ali and Sara but not Bilal; when
  saved; then total is Rs. 660, Ali Rs. 330, Sara Rs. 330, and Bilal owes
  nothing for this expense. *(Fairness: tip follows the sharers, not the
  whole group.)*

**Percentage tip rounding:**
- Given "Dinner" Rs. 1,235, tip 10%; the computed tip is Rs. 123.5, which
  rounds up to Rs. 124 (halves round up); total is Rs. 1,359.
- Given "Dinner" Rs. 1,234, tip 10%; the computed tip is Rs. 123.4, which
  rounds down to Rs. 123; total is Rs. 1,357.

**Invalid input:**
- Given the form, when I enter a flat tip of −50, then the form shows "Tip
  cannot be negative".
- Given the form, when I enter −10%, then the form shows "Tip cannot be
  negative".
- Given the form, when I enter 101%, then the form shows "Tip percentage
  cannot exceed 100%".
- Given the form, when I enter a flat tip of 99.50, then the form shows "Tip
  must be a whole number of rupees".

**Boundary values:**
- Given Rs. 500, tip exactly 100%; when saved; total is Rs. 1,000 and the
  expense is accepted.
- Given Rs. 500, tip 0%; when saved; total is Rs. 500.

**Tip causes total to exceed cap:**
- Given base Rs. 9,500,000 and flat tip Rs. 600,000 (total Rs. 10,100,000);
  then the form shows "Total including tip cannot exceed Rs. 10,000,000".
- Given base Rs. 9,500,000 and flat tip Rs. 500,000 (total Rs. 10,000,000);
  then the expense is saved.

*(Rounding when the tipped total is not evenly divisible: see S-12.)*

---

## S-6 — Edit an expense
**Serves:** J-1, J-2 | **Status:** Not implemented

As a Trip Treasurer, I want to edit a saved expense, so that I can correct
amounts, payers or participant lists after initial entry.

- Given expense "Fuel" Rs. 600; when I change the amount to Rs. 700 and save;
  then the expense shows Rs. 700.
- Given expense "Hotel" shared by Ali and Sara; when I change the sharers to
  Ali, Sara, and Bilal; then the expense shows three sharers.
- Given expense "Fuel" with payer Ali; when I change the payer to Sara; then
  the expense shows Sara as payer.
- Given the edit form; when I submit invalid input (zero amount, decimal,
  above cap, no sharers, invalid tip); then the same error messages as in S-4
  and S-5 apply and the original expense data is preserved.
- Given the settlement summary is displayed; when I save an edit; then the
  settlement recalculates automatically.

---

## S-7 — Delete an expense
**Serves:** J-1 | **Status:** Not implemented

As a Trip Treasurer, I want to delete an expense, so that I can remove entries
added by mistake.

- Given expense "Snacks" Rs. 200; when I choose to delete it and confirm; then
  "Snacks" no longer appears in the expense list.
- Given I tap delete on an expense; then the app prompts for confirmation
  before removing it — a single accidental tap does not delete the expense.
- Given I tap delete and then cancel at the confirmation prompt; then the
  expense remains unchanged.
- Given the settlement summary is displayed and I delete an expense and
  confirm; then the settlement recalculates automatically.

---

## S-8 — Persist trip data in the browser
**Serves:** J-1 | **Status:** Not implemented

As a Trip Treasurer, I want the trip data to save automatically in my browser,
so that I can close the tab or restart the browser at any point during a
multi-day trip without losing any entered data.

- Given I have added participants Ali, Sara and expense "Fuel" Rs. 600; when I
  close the tab and reopen the app in the same browser on the same device;
  then Ali, Sara and "Fuel" Rs. 600 are still present.
- Given I have entered trip data; when I restart the browser and reopen the
  app; then all participants and expenses are restored exactly as entered.
- Given I add or edit an expense; then the change is saved immediately — no
  manual "save trip" action is required.
- Given the app is opened for the first time (no data in localStorage); then
  the app starts with an empty trip and shows no error or message.
- Given localStorage contains data for this app that cannot be parsed (e.g.
  the storage was corrupted); then the app shows "Your saved trip data could
  not be loaded. Starting a new trip." and starts with an empty trip rather
  than crashing or silently discarding the data.

---

## S-9 — Start a new trip
**Serves:** J-1 | **Status:** Not implemented

As a Trip Treasurer, I want to clear all current trip data and start fresh,
so that I can use the app for a new trip without previous data interfering.

- Given the trip has participants and expenses; when I choose "Start new trip"
  and confirm; then the participant list and expense list are both empty and
  localStorage is cleared.
- Given I choose "Start new trip"; when I cancel at the confirmation prompt;
  then all participants and expenses remain intact.
- Given the trip is already empty; when I choose "Start new trip" and confirm;
  then the app remains on an empty state with no error.

---

## S-10 — View the settlement summary
**Serves:** J-3 | **Status:** Not implemented

As a Trip Treasurer, I want to see a labelled list of transfers that clears
all balances, so that the group knows exactly who pays whom and the trip is
fully settled.

**Normal cases:**
- Given Ali paid Rs. 600 for "Fuel" shared equally by Ali and Sara (each
  Rs. 300); then the settlement shows "Sara pays Ali Rs. 300".
- Given the Faisalabad scenario:
  - "Fuel to Faisalabad" Rs. 1,500, paid by Ali, shared by Ali and Usman
    (Rs. 750 each, no rounding)
  - "Fuel onwards" Rs. 2,000, paid by Usman, shared by Ali, Usman, Sara,
    Bilal (Rs. 500 each, no rounding)
  - "Hotel" Rs. 3,001, paid by Sara, shared by Ali, Usman, Sara, Bilal
    (Sara is payer and sharer — Sara Rs. 751, others Rs. 750 each per S-12)

  Net balances: Ali −Rs. 500, Usman Rs. 0, Sara +Rs. 1,750,
  Bilal −Rs. 1,250.

  Then the settlement shows: "Bilal pays Sara Rs. 1,250" and
  "Ali pays Sara Rs. 500".

- Given all net balances are zero; then the settlement shows "All balances
  are settled — no transfers needed."
- Given only one participant exists; then the settlement shows "All balances
  are settled — no transfers needed."

**Empty state:**
- Given no expenses have been added; when I view the settlement; then the app
  shows "No expenses have been added yet."

**Algorithm label:**
- The settlement section is headed "Simplified settlement" (not "Minimum
  transfers") to reflect that the greedy algorithm is not guaranteed to be
  the mathematical minimum.

**Mathematical invariant (verified by automated tests):**
- Given any set of valid expenses; when the settlement is computed; then
  applying all listed transfers to participants' net balances brings every
  balance to exactly Rs. 0.

**Continuation:**
- Given the settlement is displayed; when I add, edit or delete an expense;
  then the settlement recalculates automatically.

---

## S-11 — View the per-person breakdown
**Serves:** J-2, J-4 | **Status:** Not implemented

As a Trip Treasurer, I want to see a breakdown for each participant showing
the expenses they shared, their share of each, what they personally paid, and
their net balance, so that any group member can verify their own figure without
argument.

**Normal cases:**
- Given Ali paid Rs. 600 for "Fuel" (shared Ali, Sara — each Rs. 300), and
  Sara paid Rs. 900 for "Hotel" (shared Ali, Sara, Bilal — each Rs. 300);
  Ali's breakdown shows:
  - "Fuel": share Rs. 300, paid Rs. 600 → net from this expense: +Rs. 300
  - "Hotel": share Rs. 300, paid Rs. 0 → net from this expense: −Rs. 300
  - Summary: total paid Rs. 600, total owed Rs. 600, net balance Rs. 0
- Given Bilal was not on "Fuel"; then "Fuel" does not appear in Bilal's
  breakdown.
- Given Ali paid Rs. 300 for "Snacks" shared by Sara and Bilal only (Ali is
  payer but not a sharer); Ali's breakdown shows "Snacks": paid Rs. 300,
  share Rs. 0, net from this expense +Rs. 300.

**Consistency with settlement:**
- Given both the per-person breakdown and the settlement summary are
  displayed; then each participant's net balance in the breakdown matches
  exactly the net balance used in the settlement calculation.

**Zero balance:**
- Given a participant's total paid equals their total owed; then their
  breakdown shows net balance Rs. 0 and they do not appear in the settlement
  transfers.

*(Share values in the breakdown use the same rounded whole-rupee figures
defined in S-12.)*

---

## S-12 — See how each expense's shares were rounded
**Serves:** J-2, J-4 | **Status:** Not implemented

As a Trip Treasurer, I want to see, for each expense, how the total was
divided into whole-rupee shares and who absorbed the leftover, so that any
participant can confirm the rounding was consistent and fair.

### Canonical rounding rule
*(Referenced by S-4, S-5, S-10, S-11 — defined once here.)*

For an expense with total T (base + any rounded tip), payer P, and n sharers
listed in a fixed order:

**Case A — P is one of the n sharers:**
1. Every sharer except P receives ⌊T ÷ n⌋.
2. P receives T − (n − 1) × ⌊T ÷ n⌋. P absorbs the leftover.
3. Invariant: all n shares sum to T exactly.

**Case B — P is not one of the n sharers:**
1. Base share for each sharer: ⌊T ÷ n⌋.
2. Leftover = T − n × ⌊T ÷ n⌋ (between 0 and n − 1 rupees).
3. The first `leftover` sharers in listed order each receive one extra rupee.
4. Invariant: all n shares sum to T exactly.

**Tip rounding:** when a percentage tip is entered, the computed rupee amount
is rounded to the nearest whole rupee before being added to the base (halves
round up). The rounded total T is then divided as above.

**Shares always sum exactly to T in both cases.**

### Display placement

Rounding notes appear as a line beneath each expense in the expense list.
They are **not** repeated in the per-person breakdown (S-11).

### Zero-leftover rule

When leftover = 0 (the total divides evenly among all sharers), **no
rounding note is shown** — for both Case A and Case B.

### Acceptance criteria

**Case A — payer is a sharer:**
- Given Rs. 1,000, paid by Ali, shared by Ali → Sara → Bilal (listed order):
  Sara Rs. 333, Bilal Rs. 333, Ali Rs. 334 (absorbs Re. 1). Display shows
  "Ali absorbed Re. 1 rounding difference."
- Given Rs. 900, paid by Ali, shared by Ali → Sara → Bilal: each Rs. 300, no
  remainder. No rounding note shown.
- Given Rs. 1,001, paid by Ali, shared by Ali → Sara → Bilal: Sara Rs. 333,
  Bilal Rs. 333, Ali Rs. 335 (absorbs Rs. 2). Display shows "Ali absorbed
  Rs. 2 rounding difference."

**Case B — payer is not a sharer:**
- Given Rs. 1,000, paid by Ali (not sharing), shared by Sara → Bilal →
  Kamran: ⌊1000 ÷ 3⌋ = 333, leftover = 1. Sara Rs. 334, Bilal Rs. 333,
  Kamran Rs. 333. Sum = 1,000. Display shows "Re. 1 rounding difference added
  to Sara's share (first in listed order)."
- Given Rs. 1,001, paid by Ali (not sharing), shared by Sara → Bilal →
  Kamran: leftover = 2. Sara Rs. 334, Bilal Rs. 334, Kamran Rs. 333.
  Sum = 1,001. Display shows "Rs. 2 rounding difference distributed to Sara
  and Bilal (first in listed order)."
- Given Rs. 1,000, paid by Ali (not sharing), shared by Sara → Bilal only
  (2 sharers): 1000 ÷ 2 = 500 exactly. Sara Rs. 500, Bilal Rs. 500. No
  rounding note shown.

**Very small amounts:**
- Given Rs. 2, paid by Ali (not sharing), shared by Sara → Bilal → Kamran:
  ⌊2 ÷ 3⌋ = 0, leftover = 2. Sara Rs. 1, Bilal Rs. 1, Kamran Rs. 0.
  Sum = 2. Display shows "Rs. 2 rounding difference distributed to Sara and
  Bilal (first in listed order)." Kamran's share is Rs. 0 and still appears
  in the breakdown.

**With tip (Case A):**
- Given Rs. 1,000 + 10% tip = Rs. 1,100 total, paid by Ali (payer and
  sharer), shared by Ali → Sara → Bilal: ⌊1100 ÷ 3⌋ = 366, leftover = 2.
  Sara Rs. 366, Bilal Rs. 366, Ali Rs. 368. Display shows "Ali absorbed
  Rs. 2 rounding difference."

**Consistency:**
- The shares shown in S-12 are identical to those used in S-11 (per-person
  breakdown) and S-10 (settlement). There is one source of truth for rounding.

---

## "They must never" coverage

| Constraint from app-roles.md | Covered by |
|---|---|
| See a settlement where transfers do not account for every rupee of every net balance | S-10: mathematical invariant criterion |
| See shares on an expense that do not sum to the expense total including tip | S-12: invariant — shares sum exactly to T in both Case A and Case B |
| Lose entered data without an explicit confirmation step | S-7: delete confirmation; S-9: new-trip confirmation; S-8: corrupt-data message instead of silent discard |
| Remove a participant who is named on one or more expenses — app blocks and names the expenses | S-3: blocked-as-sharer, blocked-as-payer, multi-expense message |
| Submit an expense with no participants sharing it | S-4: "At least one participant must share this expense" |
| Enter a zero or negative expense amount | S-4: "Amount must be greater than zero" |
| Add a participant with an empty or duplicate name | S-1: empty-name and duplicate criteria; S-2: same on rename |
| Enter an amount that is not a whole number of rupees | S-4: "Amount must be a whole number of rupees"; S-5: "Tip must be a whole number of rupees" |
| Enter a single expense amount above Rs. 10,000,000 | S-4: boundary criteria; S-5: total-including-tip cap |
| Enter a negative tip, or a percentage tip above 100% | S-5: negative-tip and >100% criteria |

input.content:
# Trip Expense Splitter

A browser-based calculator that tracks shared expenses across a group trip and produces a settlement showing who pays whom. Built as a take-home assignment for KnowledgeCity (Technology Division).

---

## Running the app

**Requirements:** Node 20 or later. No accounts, API keys or cloud services needed.

```bash
npm install      # install dependencies (first time only)
npm run dev      # start local dev server → open http://localhost:5173
```

### Running tests

```bash
npm test         # run unit tests once and exit
```

### Production build (optional)

```bash
npm run build    # outputs to dist/
npm run preview  # serve the production build locally
```

---

## What it does

Add trip participants, record shared expenses (who paid, who shares, optional tip), and get:

- A **simplified settlement** listing who pays whom to clear all debts.
- A **per-person breakdown** showing each participant's share of every expense, what they paid, and their net balance — so anyone can verify the numbers.

Data is saved automatically to the browser's local storage. Closing the tab and reopening restores your trip. Use **New Trip** to clear everything and start again.

---

## Key assumptions

The following assumptions were made during discovery (no real user interviews were conducted):

- **A1** — Users enter expenses on the same device and browser throughout the trip. Data survives tab closure; it does not survive clearing browser storage or switching device.
- **A2** — One person acts as treasurer and does all data entry. Simultaneous multi-user input is not supported.
- **A3** — Equal-per-participant splitting is the dominant rule. Item-level splits within a single bill are out of scope for v1.
- **A4** — Users prefer a purpose-built browser tool over a phone calculator for multi-expense trips. This is the core adoption risk: users who feel enough pain may already use dedicated expense-sharing apps, and those who don't may not adopt a new tool either.
- **A5** — Greedy settlement (≤ N−1 transfers) is acceptable. Users do not need a mathematically optimal minimum.
- **A6** — All amounts are in Pakistani Rupees. No multi-currency support.

---

## Manual changes

*None so far. If you edit code by hand, log the change here with a date and description.*

---

## Architecture

```
src/
  logic/          Pure TypeScript — no DOM, fully unit tested
    types.ts      Domain types (Participant, Expense, TipInput, …)
    validation.ts Input validation (returns error strings or null)
    tip.ts        Tip calculation and percentage rounding
    rounding.ts   Whole-rupee share splitting (S-12 canonical rule)
    balances.ts   Net balance computation per participant
    settlement.ts Greedy debtor-creditor settlement algorithm
    storage.ts    localStorage load/save (takes a StorageBackend parameter)
  ui/
    state.ts      App state singleton
    utils.ts      escHtml, formatRs, newId

# Trip Expense Splitter

A browser-based calculator that tracks shared expenses across a group trip and produces a settlement showing who pays whom. Built as a take-home assignment for KnowledgeCity (Technology Division).

---

## Running the app

**Requirements:** Node 20 or later. No accounts, API keys or cloud services needed.

```bash
npm install      # install dependencies (first time only)
npm run dev      # start local dev server → open http://localhost:5173
```

### Running tests

```bash
npm test         # run unit tests once and exit
```

### Production build (optional)

```bash
npm run build    # outputs to dist/
npm run preview  # serve the production build locally
```

---

## What it does

Add trip participants, record shared expenses (who paid, who shares, optional tip), and get:

- A **simplified settlement** listing who pays whom to clear all debts.
- A **per-person breakdown** showing each participant's share of every expense, what they paid, and their net balance — so anyone can verify the numbers.

Data is saved automatically to the browser's local storage. Closing the tab and reopening restores your trip. Use **New Trip** to clear everything and start again.

---

## Key assumptions

The following assumptions were made during discovery (no real user interviews were conducted):

- **A1** — Users enter expenses on the same device and browser throughout the trip. Data survives tab closure; it does not survive clearing browser storage or switching device.
- **A2** — One person acts as treasurer and does all data entry. Simultaneous multi-user input is not supported.
- **A3** — Equal-per-participant splitting is the dominant rule. Item-level splits within a single bill are out of scope for v1.
- **A4** — Users prefer a purpose-built browser tool over a phone calculator for multi-expense trips. This is the core adoption risk: users who feel enough pain may already use dedicated expense-sharing apps, and those who don't may not adopt a new tool either.
- **A5** — Greedy settlement (≤ N−1 transfers) is acceptable. Users do not need a mathematically optimal minimum.
- **A6** — All amounts are in Pakistani Rupees. No multi-currency support.

---

## Manual changes

*None so far. If you edit code by hand, log the change here with a date and description.*

---

## Architecture

```
src/
  logic/          Pure TypeScript — no DOM, fully unit tested
    types.ts      Domain types (Participant, Expense, TipInput, …)
    validation.ts Input validation (returns error strings or null)
    tip.ts        Tip calculation and percentage rounding
    rounding.ts   Whole-rupee share splitting (S-12 canonical rule)
    balances.ts   Net balance computation per participant
    settlement.ts Greedy debtor-creditor settlement algorithm
    storage.ts    localStorage load/save (takes a StorageBackend parameter)
  ui/
    state.ts      App state singleton
    utils.ts      escHtml, formatRs, newId
    app.ts        Render loop + all event handlers
    sections/     One file per UI section (render + bind)
  main.ts         Entry point
  style.css       Styles
```

The logic layer has zero DOM access and zero side effects. All calculation functions take plain data in and return plain data out. Storage takes a `StorageBackend` interface so tests can use an in-memory fake.

message.content:
79 manual checks is too many for the time budget, so let's split
verification:

1. Add Playwright end-to-end tests that drive the real UI for every
acceptance criterion where that's practical. Name each test after its
story and criterion like the unit tests. Add it as a separate script,
"npm run test:e2e", so "npm test" stays fast and simple for reviewers.
Document in the README that e2e needs a one-time browser download.

2. Replace docs/qa-checklist.md with 10 to 12 manual scenarios that each
walk through a realistic flow and cover as many criteria as possible
(e.g. the full Faisalabad trip). For each scenario, list which criteria
it covers. Every story must be covered by at least one scenario.

3. Run the e2e suite and show me the results. Don't change any statuses
yet. I'll do the manual scenarios, then we'll update statuses together
based on both.

P.S. note for reviewer: this prompt is generated from calude desktop since 78 tests are too many for manual testing

content.thinking:
Let me plan this carefully.

1. **Playwright E2E tests** - Need to:
   - Install Playwright
   - Create e2e test files covering all acceptance criteria that are practical to test via UI
   - Add `test:e2e` script to package.json
   - Document in README

2. **Replace qa-checklist with 10-12 manual scenarios** - Create a new focused manual checklist with realistic flows

3. **Run the e2e suite** and show results

Let me think about what's practical to test in Playwright vs what needs manual testing:
- Most UI interactions can be automated
- S-8 (storage persistence across browser restart) - can test tab close/reopen with Playwright but browser restart is harder; can test localStorage directly
- I can also manipulate localStorage directly to simulate corruption, and the Faisalabad scenario's calculations are fully automatable too.

Now I'm mapping out which scenarios to automate in Playwright: adding, renaming, and removing participants, adding and editing expenses, handling tips, and so on -- each with their full set of acceptance criteria covered.

Delete expense, new trip, settlement, breakdown, and rounding scenarios all look fully automatable too. The persistence scenario (S-8) has some trickier parts -- simulating a tab close/reopen is easy enough by navigating away and back, but a true browser restart is harder to replicate, though first-run and corrupt-storage cases are still doable. Overall almost everything is automatable, with S-8's browser-restart case being the main exception.

Now I'm sketching out the test file organization, deciding whether to group spec files by story number or by feature cluster, and leaning toward grouping by feature area to keep things manageable -- something like participants, expenses, persistence, and settlement spec files.

Writing helper functions...

For tab close/reopen persistence tests, I'm planning to use a single browser context, add data, close just the page, then open a new page within the same context to verify the data survived. For simulating a full browser restart, I need to be careful since Playwright's default `browser.newContext()` creates isolated profiles that won't share localStorage -- I'd need `launchPersistentContext` with a shared user data directory to truly simulate persistence across sessions.

Actually, I realize `page.reload()` is the simplest way to test this: add data, reload the page, then check it's still there, which effectively validates localStorage persistence without needing a full context teardown. Now I'm also thinking about how to select sharers by name for the Faisalabad scenario, looking at how the sharer checkboxes are structured in the UI.

Since the checkboxes are labeled with participant names, I can target them directly by their visible label text in Playwright, and similarly for the payer dropdown I can select by the option's text label since it matches the participant name. Now I'm setting up the Playwright config file to define the test directory and environment.

I want it to automatically spin up the Vite dev server when e2e tests run, reusing an existing server if one's already active, and I'll install just the Chromium browser to keep things fast. Now I'm sketching out the manual test checklist, aiming for 10-12 scenarios covering all the user stories -- starting with a simple two-person dinner split and settlement, then building toward a fuller multi-participant trip scenario with several expenses.

I'm continuing to lay out the remaining scenarios: tip handling and rounding, roster management with guardrails, editing/deleting expenses and verifying settlement updates, payers excluded from splits, error handling for bad inputs, browser persistence including corrupted storage recovery, and finally starting a new trip scenario.

Now I'm thinking through which of the 12 scenarios naturally map to automated Playwright tests versus manual checks, concluding most things like UI text and rounding behavior are automatable, leaving only true browser-restart edge cases as genuinely hard to automate.

I'm mapping out that nearly all the acceptance criteria across S-1 through S-12, including the Faisalabad scenario and storage edge cases, can be covered by Playwright automation, leaving only a few true manual checks like genuine browser restarts and cross-browser visual verification.

The user is asking why Sohaib doesn't pay Ashar 5,000 and Zubair 3,750 directly, instead of paying Zubair 8,750. Let me explain the greedy algorithm clearly.

The user's intuition is correct from a "who owes whom directly" perspective. But the greedy algorithm looks at NET balances, not individual expense-by-expense debts.

Sohaib's debts:
- Owes Ashar Rs. 5,000 (from expense 1)
- Owes Zubair Rs. 3,750 (from expense 2)
- Total: Rs. 8,750

The algorithm computes that Ashar is only NET owed Rs. 1,250, since Ashar himself owes Zubair Rs. 3,750. So rather than Sohaib paying Ashar 5,000 and Ashar separately paying Zubair 3,750, it's more efficient to route Sohaib's payment straight to Zubair, cutting out a transaction. If Sohaib paid Ashar directly, Ashar would then have to forward 3,750 to Zubair anyway.

Comparing approaches: the greedy method has Sohaib pay Zubair 8,750, Hamza pay Zubair 2,500, and Hamza pay Ashar 1,250 — three transactions total. The naive per-expense method also lands at three transactions (Sohaib→Ashar 5,000, Sohaib→Zubair 3,750, Hamza→Zubair 3,750), so the transaction count ends up matching in this case.

Sohaib simply skips the middleman and pays Zubair directly, landing everyone at a zero net balance with fewer transactions. The user's original proposal (Sohaib pays Ashar 5,000, then Sohaib pays Zubair 3,750) is also a valid settlement—it just takes 4 transfers instead of 3.

content.text:
Your intuition is correct that **Sohaib directly caused those debts** — 5,000 to Ashar and 3,750 to Zubair. That would be 4 total transfers across the whole trip:

1. Sohaib → Ashar: 5,000
2. Sohaib → Zubair: 3,750
3. Hamza → Zubair: 3,750
4. **Ashar → Zubair: 3,750** ← this extra one is why the greedy skips it

The greedy algorithm looks at **net balances first**, then settles:

- Ashar is owed 5,000 by Sohaib, but *also owes* 3,750 to Zubair himself. His net is only **+1,250**.
- So instead of Sohaib → Ashar (5,000) and then Ashar → Zubair (3,750), the algorithm says: Sohaib, skip the middleman and just pay Zubair directly. Sohaib's total debt is 8,750 either way.

This brings transfers from **4 down to 3**, and every net balance still reaches zero:

| Person | Net | Receives | Pays | Result |
|--------|-----|----------|------|--------|
| Zubair | +11,250 | 8,750 + 2,500 | — | 0 ✓ |
| Ashar | +1,250 | 1,250 (from Hamza) | — | 0 ✓ |
| Sohaib | −8,750 | — | 8,750 | 0 ✓ |
| Hamza | −3,750 | — | 2,500 + 1,250 | 0 ✓ |

So your approach would also be **mathematically correct** — it's just one extra bank transfer. The greedy settlement trades directness for fewer transactions, which is the documented behaviour (the CLAUDE.md and docs call it "simplified settlement" and note it's not guaranteed to match the intuitive per-payer breakdown, just that all balances clear). Neither result is wrong.

# Manual QA Scenarios

Ten scenario-based walkthroughs for acceptance criteria that are best verified by hand: genuine browser restart, cross-browser checks, and complex multi-step flows that span several stories. Run these after the automated Playwright suite passes. Mark each scenario Pass or Fail and note the browser and date.

Automated coverage: the Playwright suite in `e2e/` covers all acceptance criteria that can be driven programmatically. These scenarios cover the remainder and add end-to-end confidence across real browser sessions.

---

## Scenario 1 — Faisalabad trip end-to-end

**Covers:** S-1.1, S-1.2, S-4.1, S-4.2, S-10.2, S-10.6, S-11.1, S-11.2, S-11.4, S-12.1, S-12.2, S-12.9, S-12.10, S-12.11

**Setup:** Open the app in a fresh state (no prior data). Use "New Trip" to clear if needed.

**Steps:**

1. Add participants: Ali, Usman, Sara, Bilal.
2. Click "+ Add Expense". Enter: description "Fuel to Faisalabad", amount 1500, payer Ali, sharers Ali and Usman. Save.
3. Add a second expense: description "Fuel onwards", amount 2000, payer Usman, sharers Ali, Usman, Sara, Bilal. Save.
4. Add a third expense: description "Hotel", amount 3001, payer Sara, sharers Ali, Usman, Sara, Bilal. Save.
5. Scroll to the "Simplified settlement" section.
6. Scroll to the "Per-person breakdown" section and review each person's table.
7. Look under the "Fuel to Faisalabad" expense item for any rounding note.
8. Look under the "Hotel" expense item for a rounding note.
9. In the breakdown, sum all four share figures shown for Hotel.

**Expected results:**

- After step 1: all four names appear in the participant list.
- After step 4: three expenses visible with correct descriptions, amounts, payers, and sharers.
- Step 5: settlement section heading reads "Simplified settlement" (not "Minimum transfers"). Exactly two transfer rows appear: "Bilal pays Sara Rs. 1,250" and "Ali pays Sara Rs. 500". No other transfers.
- Step 6: Ali's breakdown shows Fuel to Faisalabad (share Rs. 750, paid Rs. 1,500) and Fuel onwards (share Rs. 500, paid Rs. 0) and Hotel (share Rs. 750, paid Rs. 0). Net balance Rs. 0 — Ali does not appear as a payer in the settlement. Bilal's breakdown does not contain "Fuel to Faisalabad".
- Step 7: No rounding note under "Fuel to Faisalabad" (1,500 ÷ 2 = 750 exactly).
- Step 8: Rounding note appears under "Hotel": "Sara absorbed Re. 1 rounding difference." The same note does NOT appear anywhere inside the per-person breakdown tables.
- Step 9: The four Hotel share values (from each person's breakdown row) sum to exactly 3,001.

---

4. Add expense "Fuel" Rs. 600, paid by Ali, sharers Ali and Sara.
5. Rename Ali to "Ali Khan". Click Rename on Ali, type "Ali Khan", click Save.
6. Open the edit form for "Fuel" and check the payer dropdown and sharer checkboxes.
7. Try to rename Sara to "ali khan" — observe the error.
8. Try to rename Sara to "sara" (different case) — observe the result.
9. Try to remove Ali Khan — observe the error.
10. Add expense "Hotel" Rs. 900, paid by Ali Khan, sharers Ali Khan and Sara.
11. Try to remove Ali Khan again — observe the error message.
12. Edit "Fuel": uncheck Ali Khan from sharers and change payer to Sara. Save.
13. Edit "Hotel": uncheck Ali Khan from sharers and change payer to Sara. Save.
14. Remove Ali Khan.

**Expected results:**

- Step 2: "A participant named Ali already exists". No duplicate added.
- Step 3: "Name cannot be empty". No participant added.
- Step 5: Roster shows "Ali Khan". The "Fuel" expense now shows "Ali Khan" as payer and sharer in the edit form.
- Step 7: "A participant named Ali Khan already exists". Sara's name unchanged.
- Step 8: Rename accepted without error; Sara's name updates to "sara" (or same case entered).

- Step 11: Error lists both expenses: "...they appear on "Fuel" and "Hotel". Update those expenses first."
- Step 14: Ali Khan removed successfully; roster shows only Sara (or "sara") and Bilal.

- Step 2: "Dinner" shows Rs. 1,359 (not Rs. 1,358.50 — the tip Rs. 123.5 rounds up to Rs. 124, total = Rs. 1,235 + Rs. 124 = Rs. 1,359).
- Step 3: Ali's share of Dinner is Rs. 680 (Ali absorbs the Rs. 1 leftover: ⌊1359 ÷ 2⌋ = 679, Ali gets 680). Sara's share is Rs. 679. (Or Ali Rs. 679, Sara Rs. 680 depending on listed order — both sum to 1,359.)
- Step 4: Rounding note visible under "Dinner" expense item.
- Step 5: No rounding note text appears inside the per-person breakdown section.
- Step 7: "Lunch" shows Rs. 660 (600 + 60 flat tip).

1. Add participants: Ali, Usman, Sara, Bilal.

3. Add a second expense: description "Fuel onwards", amount 2000, payer Usman, sharers Ali, Usman, Sara, Bilal. Save.
4. Add a third expense: description "Hotel", amount 3001, payer Sara, sharers Ali, Usman, Sara, Bilal. Save.

**Covers:** S-1.3, S-1.4, S-1.5, S-1.6, S-2.2, S-2.3, S-2.6, S-3.2, S-3.3, S-4.3, S-4.4, S-4.5, S-4.6, S-4.7, S-4.8, S-4.11, S-4.13, S-5.7, S-5.8, S-5.9, S-5.10, S-5.13

**Steps:**

2. Try to add participant with whitespace-only name "   ". Correct and add "Sara".
3. Try to add "ali" (duplicate). Correct and add "Bilal".
4. Rename Ali: try empty name. Correct with a valid name "Kamran". Confirm success.
5. Rename Sara: try to rename to "Bilal". Correct with "Sara Khan". Confirm success.
6. Add expense "Fuel" Rs. 600, payer Kamran, sharers Kamran and Sara Khan.
7. Try to remove Kamran. Observe block message naming "Fuel".
8. Add expense "Snacks" Rs. 200, payer Bilal, sharers Sara Khan (Bilal is payer but not sharer).
9. Try to remove Bilal. Observe block message naming "Snacks".
10. Open the Add Expense form. Try each of the following in turn (correct after each error before trying the next):
    - Submit with empty description.
    - Enter amount 0.
    - Enter amount −500.
    - Enter amount 999.50 (decimal).
    - Uncheck all sharers, submit.
    - Leave payer unselected, submit.
    - Enter amount 10,000,001.
11. Correct all fields and save — confirm the expense is saved and no error remains.
12. Add another expense. Try each tip error:
    - Select "Flat amount", enter −50. Submit.
    - Change to −10% percentage. Submit.
    - Enter 101%. Submit.
    - Select "Flat amount", enter 99.50. Submit.
    - Enter base 9,500,000 with flat tip 600,000. Submit.
13. Correct the tip and save. Confirm success.

**Expected results:**

Each invalid submission shows exactly the error message specified in `docs/user-stories.md` for that criterion. After each correction and resubmission, the error disappears and the action succeeds. No submission with invalid data is ever persisted. The app never crashes or freezes at any point in the sweep.

Exact error messages to verify:
- Empty/whitespace name: "Name cannot be empty"
- Duplicate name: "A participant named [Name] already exists"
- Remove blocked by expense: "Cannot remove [Name]: they appear on [Expense]. Update that expense first."
- Empty description: "Description cannot be empty"
- Amount ≤ 0: "Amount must be greater than zero"
- Decimal amount: "Amount must be a whole number of rupees"
- No sharers: "At least one participant must share this expense"
- No payer: "A payer must be selected"
- Amount above cap: "Amount cannot exceed Rs. 10,000,000"
- Negative tip: "Tip cannot be negative"
- Tip percentage > 100%: "Tip percentage cannot exceed 100%"
- Decimal flat tip: "Tip must be a whole number of rupees"
- Total with tip above cap: "Total including tip cannot exceed Rs. 10,000,000"

- Step 2: "Min" saved and visible at Rs. 1. No error.
- Step 3: "Max" saved and visible at Rs. 10,000,000. No error.
- Step 4: All share values display as whole numbers (e.g., "3,333,334" and "3,333,333"). No value uses scientific notation (no "e+" or "e−").
- Step 5: Error "Amount cannot exceed Rs. 10,000,000".
- Step 7: Total is Rs. 500 (0% tip adds nothing).
- Step 9: Total is Rs. 1,000 (100% tip doubles the base).
- Step 10: "TipExact" saved at Rs. 10,000,000. No error.
- Step 11: Error "Total including tip cannot exceed Rs. 10,000,000".

Ten scenario-based walkthroughs for acceptance criteria that are best verified by hand: genuine browser restart, cross-browser checks, and complex multi-step flows that span several stories. Run these after the automated Playwright suite passes. Mark each scenario Pass or Fail and note the browser and date.

Automated coverage: the Playwright suite in `e2e/` covers all acceptance criteria that can be driven programmatically. These scenarios cover the remainder and add end-to-end confidence across real browser sessions.

## Scenario 1 — Faisalabad trip end-to-end

**Covers:** S-1.1, S-1.2, S-4.1, S-4.2, S-10.2, S-10.6, S-11.1, S-11.2, S-11.4, S-12.1, S-12.2, S-12.9, S-12.10, S-12.11

**Setup:** Open the app in a fresh state (no prior data). Use "New Trip" to clear if needed.

**Steps:**

1. Add participants: Ali, Usman, Sara, Bilal.
2. Click "+ Add Expense". Enter: description "Fuel to Faisalabad", amount 1500, payer Ali, sharers Ali and Usman. Save.
3. Add a second expense: description "Fuel onwards", amount 2000, payer Usman, sharers Ali, Usman, Sara, Bilal. Save.
4. Add a third expense: description "Hotel", amount 3001, payer Sara, sharers Ali, Usman, Sara, Bilal. Save.
5. Scroll to the "Simplified settlement" section.
6. Scroll to the "Per-person breakdown" section and review each person's table.
7. Look under the "Fuel to Faisalabad" expense item for any rounding note.
8. Look under the "Hotel" expense item for a rounding note.

**Expected results:**

- After step 1: all four names appear in the participant list.
- After step 4: three expenses visible with correct descriptions, amounts, payers, and sharers.
- Step 5: settlement section heading reads "Simplified settlement" (not "Minimum transfers"). Exactly two transfer rows appear: "Bilal pays Sara Rs. 1,250" and "Ali pays Sara Rs. 500". No other transfers.

Ten scenario-based walkthroughs for acceptance criteria that are best verified by hand: genuine browser restart, cross-browser checks, and complex multi-step flows that span several stories. Automated coverage: the Playwright suite in `e2e/` covers all acceptance criteria that can be driven programmatically. These scenarios cover the remainder and add end-to-end confidence across real browser sessions.

## Scenario 1 — Faisalabad trip end-to-end

**Covers:** S-1.1, S-1.2, S-4.1, S-4.2, S-10.2, S-10.6, S-11.1, S-11.2, S-11.4, S-12.1, S-12.2, S-12.9, S-12.10, S-12.11

   336→## S-12 — See how each expense's shares were rounded
   337→**Serves:** J-2, J-4 | **Status:** Not implemented
   338→
   339→As a Trip Treasurer, I want to see, for each expense, how the total was
   340→divided into whole-rupee shares and who absorbed the leftover, so that any
   341→participant can confirm the rounding was consistent and fair.
   342→
   343→### Canonical rounding rule
   344→*(Referenced by S-4, S-5, S-10, S-11 — defined once here.)*
   345→
   346→For an expense with total T (base + any rounded tip), payer P, and n sharers
   347→listed in a fixed order:
   348→
   349→**Case A — P is one of the n sharers:**
   350→1. Every sharer except P receives ⌊T ÷ n⌋.
   351→2. P receives T − (n − 1) × ⌊T ÷ n⌋. P absorbs the leftover.
   352→3. Invariant: all n shares sum to T exactly.
   353→
   354→**Case B — P is not one of the n sharers:**
   355→1. Base share for each sharer: ⌊T ÷ n⌋.
   356→2. Leftover = T − n × ⌊T ÷ n⌋ (between 0 and n − 1 rupees).
   357→3. The first `leftover` sharers in listed order each receive one extra rupee.
   358→4. Invariant: all n shares sum to T exactly.
   359→
   360→**Tip rounding:** when a percentage tip is entered, the computed rupee amount
   361→is rounded to the nearest whole rupee before being added to the base (halves
   362→round up). The rounded total T is then divided as above.
   363→
   364→**Shares always sum exactly to T in both cases.**
   365→
   366→### Display placement
   367→
   368→Rounding notes appear as a line beneath each expense in the expense list.
   369→They are **not** repeated in the per-person breakdown (S-11).
   370→
   371→### Zero-leftover rule
   372→
   373→When leftover = 0 (the total divides evenly among all sharers), **no
   374→rounding note is shown** — for both Case A and Case B.
   375→
   376→### Acceptance criteria

   378→**Case A — payer is a sharer:**

   381→  "Ali absorbed Re. 1 rounding difference."
   382→- Given Rs. 900, paid by Ali, shared by Ali → Sara → Bilal: each Rs. 300, no
   383→  remainder. No rounding note shown.
   384→- Given Rs. 1,001, paid by Ali, shared by Ali → Sara → Bilal: Sara Rs. 333,
   385→  Bilal Rs. 333, Ali Rs. 335 (absorbs Rs. 2). Display shows "Ali absorbed
   386→  Rs. 2 rounding difference."
   387→
   388→**Case B — payer is not a sharer:**
   389→- Given Rs. 1,000, paid by Ali (not sharing), shared by Sara → Bilal →
   390→  Kamran: ⌊1000 ÷ 3⌋ = 333, leftover = 1. Sara Rs. 334, Bilal Rs. 333,
   391→  Kamran Rs. 333. Sum = 1,000. Display shows "Re. 1 rounding difference added
   392→  to Sara's share (first in listed order)."
   393→- Given Rs. 1,001, paid by Ali (not sharing), shared by Sara → Bilal →
   394→  Kamran: leftover = 2. Sara Rs. 334, Bilal Rs. 334, Kamran Rs. 333.
   395→  Sum = 1,001. Display shows "Rs. 2 rounding difference distributed to Sara
   396→  and Bilal (first in listed order)."
   397→- Given Rs. 1,000, paid by Ali (not sharing), shared by Sara → Bilal only
   398→  (2 sharers): 1000 ÷ 2 = 500 exactly. Sara Rs. 500, Bilal Rs. 500. No
   399→  rounding note shown.
   400→
   401→**Very small amounts:**
   402→- Given Rs. 2, paid by Ali (not sharing), shared by Sara → Bilal → Kamran:
   403→  ⌊2 ÷ 3⌋ = 0, leftover = 2. Sara Rs. 1, Bilal Rs. 1, Kamran Rs. 0.
   404→  Sum = 2. Display shows "Rs. 2 rounding difference distributed to Sara and
   405→  Bilal (first in listed order)." Kamran's share is Rs. 0 and still appears
   406→  in the breakdown.
   407→
   408→**With tip (Case A):**

# User Stories

*Statuses updated after each story is built and verified against its acceptance criteria.*

---

## S-1 — Add a participant
**Serves:** J-1 | **Status:** Not implemented

As a Trip Treasurer, I want to add a named participant to the trip, so that
they can be assigned as payers or included in expense splits.

- Given an empty roster, when I type "Ali" and confirm, then "Ali" appears
  in the participant list.
- Given "Ali" is already in the roster, when I add "Sara", then both appear
  in the list.
- Given the add-participant form, when I submit an empty name (or a name of
  only spaces), then the form shows "Name cannot be empty" and no participant
  is added.
- Given "Ali" is in the roster, when I try to add "Ali" (same name,
  case-insensitive), then the form shows "A participant named Ali already
  exists" and no duplicate is added.
- Given the form shows an error, when I enter a valid unique name and confirm,
  then the participant is added and the error clears.

---

## S-2 — Rename a participant
**Serves:** J-1 | **Status:** Not implemented

As a Trip Treasurer, I want to rename a participant, so that I can correct a
typo or name change without losing their expense data.

- Given "Ali" is in the roster, when I rename them to "Ali Khan" and confirm,
  then "Ali Khan" appears in the list and all expenses that referenced "Ali"
  now reference "Ali Khan".
- Given the rename form, when I submit an empty name, then the form shows
  "Name cannot be empty" and the name is unchanged.
- Given "Ali" and "Sara" are in the roster, when I rename "Ali" to "Sara",
  then the form shows "A participant named Sara already exists" and the name
  is unchanged.
- Given "Ali" is in the roster, when I rename "Ali" to "Ali" (no change),
  then the form is accepted without error.
- Given "Ali" is in the roster, when I rename "Ali" to "ali" (same name,
  different case), then the form is accepted without error and the
  participant's name is updated to "ali".
- Given the form shows an error, when I enter a valid unique name and confirm,
  then the rename succeeds and the error clears.

---

## S-3 — Remove a participant
**Serves:** J-1 | **Status:** Not implemented

As a Trip Treasurer, I want to remove a participant from the trip, so that I
can correct mistakes in the group setup.

- Given "Ali" is in the roster and not named on any expense (neither as payer
  nor sharer), when I remove "Ali", then "Ali" no longer appears in the
  participant list.
- Given "Ali" is a sharer on "Fuel to Faisalabad", when I try to remove
  "Ali", then the app shows "Cannot remove Ali: they appear on Fuel to
  Faisalabad. Update that expense first." and Ali remains in the roster.
- Given "Ali" is the payer on "Snacks" but not a sharer on that expense, when
  I try to remove "Ali", then the app shows "Cannot remove Ali: they appear on
  Snacks. Update that expense first." and Ali remains.
- Given "Ali" appears on both "Fuel" and "Hotel", when I try to remove "Ali",
  then the message lists both: "Cannot remove Ali: they appear on Fuel and
  Hotel. Update those expenses first."
- Given Ali has been removed from all expenses they were named on, when I
  remove "Ali", then the removal succeeds.

---

## S-4 — Add an expense
**Serves:** J-1, J-2 | **Status:** Not implemented

As a Trip Treasurer, I want to add an expense with a description, total
amount, payer, and the subset of participants sharing it, so that I can record
exactly what was spent, who paid, and which members the cost applies to.

**Normal cases:**
- Given participants Ali, Sara, Bilal; when I save "Fuel" Rs. 900, paid by
  Ali, shared by Ali and Sara; then the expense shows description "Fuel",
  amount Rs. 900, payer Ali, sharers Ali and Sara.
- Given participants Ali, Sara, Bilal; when I save "Snacks" Rs. 300, paid by
  Ali, shared by Sara and Bilal (Ali is payer but not a sharer); then the
  expense is saved with Ali as payer and Sara and Bilal as the only sharers.

**Invalid input:**
- Given the form, when I submit with no description, then the form shows
  "Description cannot be empty" and no expense is saved.
- Given the form, when I enter amount 0, then the form shows "Amount must be
  greater than zero".
- Given the form, when I enter a negative amount (e.g. −500), then the form
  shows "Amount must be greater than zero".
- Given the form, when I enter 999.50, then the form shows "Amount must be a
  whole number of rupees".
- Given the form, when I select zero sharers, then the form shows "At least
  one participant must share this expense".
- Given the form, when I submit without selecting a payer, then the form shows
  "A payer must be selected".

**Boundary values:**
- Given the form, when I enter 1 (minimum valid amount), then the expense is
  saved.
- Given the form, when I enter Rs. 10,000,000, then the expense is saved.
- Given the form, when I enter Rs. 10,000,001, then the form shows "Amount
  cannot exceed Rs. 10,000,000".

**Large numbers:**
- Given Rs. 10,000,000 shared equally among 3 participants; when saved; then
  all shares display as whole-rupee figures and no value is shown in scientific
  notation.

**Continuation after error:**
- Given the form shows a validation error, when I correct all fields and
  resubmit, then the expense is saved and the error clears.

*(How shares are divided into whole rupees: see S-12. S-4 applies that rule;
it is not repeated here.)*

---

## S-5 — Add a tip to an expense
**Serves:** J-1, J-2 | **Status:** Not implemented

As a Trip Treasurer, I want to attach a tip to an expense as a whole
percentage or a flat rupee amount, so that the full amount actually paid is
included in each participant's share.

**Normal cases:**
- Given "Dinner" Rs. 1,000, tip 10%, shared equally by Ali and Sara; when
  saved; then total is Rs. 1,100 and each share is Rs. 550.
- Given "Dinner" Rs. 1,000, flat tip Rs. 100, shared equally by Ali and Sara;
  when saved; then total is Rs. 1,100 and each share is Rs. 550.
- Given "Fuel" Rs. 800, tip field left blank; when saved; then total is
  Rs. 800 (no tip applied).
- Given "Lunch" Rs. 600, tip 10%, shared by Ali and Sara but not Bilal; when
  saved; then total is Rs. 660, Ali Rs. 330, Sara Rs. 330, and Bilal owes
  nothing for this expense. *(Fairness: tip follows the sharers, not the
  whole group.)*

**Percentage tip rounding:**
- Given "Dinner" Rs. 1,235, tip 10%; the computed tip is Rs. 123.5, which
  rounds up to Rs. 124 (halves round up); total is Rs. 1,359.
- Given "Dinner" Rs. 1,234, tip 10%; the computed tip is Rs. 123.4, which
  rounds down to Rs. 123; total is Rs. 1,357.

**Invalid input:**
- Given the form, when I enter a flat tip of −50, then the form shows "Tip
  cannot be negative".
- Given the form, when I enter −10%, then the form shows "Tip cannot be
  negative".
- Given the form, when I enter 101%, then the form shows "Tip percentage
  cannot exceed 100%".
- Given the form, when I enter a flat tip of 99.50, then the form shows "Tip
  must be a whole number of rupees".

**Boundary values:**
- Given Rs. 500, tip exactly 100%; when saved; total is Rs. 1,000 and the
  expense is accepted.
- Given Rs. 500, tip 0%; when saved; total is Rs. 500.

**Tip causes total to exceed cap:**
- Given base Rs. 9,500,000 and flat tip Rs. 600,000 (total Rs. 10,100,000);
  then the form shows "Total including tip cannot exceed Rs. 10,000,000".
- Given base Rs. 9,500,000 and flat tip Rs. 500,000 (total Rs. 10,000,000);
  then the expense is saved.

*(Rounding when the tipped total is not evenly divisible: see S-12.)*

---

## S-6 — Edit an expense
**Serves:** J-1, J-2 | **Status:** Not implemented

As a Trip Treasurer, I want to edit a saved expense, so that I can correct
amounts, payers or participant lists after initial entry.

- Given expense "Fuel" Rs. 600; when I change the amount to Rs. 700 and save;
  then the expense shows Rs. 700.
- Given expense "Hotel" shared by Ali and Sara; when I change the sharers to
  Ali, Sara, and Bilal; then the expense shows three sharers.
- Given expense "Fuel" with payer Ali; when I change the payer to Sara; then
  the expense shows Sara as payer.
- Given the edit form; when I submit invalid input (zero amount, decimal,
  above cap, no sharers, invalid tip); then the same error messages as in S-4
  and S-5 apply and the original expense data is preserved.
- Given the settlement summary is displayed; when I save an edit; then the
  settlement recalculates automatically.

---

## S-7 — Delete an expense
**Serves:** J-1 | **Status:** Not implemented

As a Trip Treasurer, I want to delete an expense, so that I can remove entries
added by mistake.

- Given expense "Snacks" Rs. 200; when I choose to delete it and confirm; then
  "Snacks" no longer appears in the expense list.
- Given I tap delete on an expense; then the app prompts for confirmation
  before removing it — a single accidental tap does not delete the expense.
- Given I tap delete and then cancel at the confirmation prompt; then the
  expense remains unchanged.
- Given the settlement summary is displayed and I delete an expense and
  confirm; then the settlement recalculates automatically.

---

## S-8 — Persist trip data in the browser
**Serves:** J-1 | **Status:** Not implemented

As a Trip Treasurer, I want the trip data to save automatically in my browser,
so that I can close the tab or restart the browser at any point during a
multi-day trip without losing any entered data.

- Given I have added participants Ali, Sara and expense "Fuel" Rs. 600; when I
  close the tab and reopen the app in the same browser on the same device;
  then Ali, Sara and "Fuel" Rs. 600 are still present.
- Given I have entered trip data; when I restart the browser and reopen the
  app; then all participants and expenses are restored exactly as entered.
- Given I add or edit an expense; then the change is saved immediately — no
  manual "save trip" action is required.
- Given the app is opened for the first time (no data in localStorage); then
  the app starts with an empty trip and shows no error or message.
- Given localStorage contains data for this app that cannot be parsed (e.g.
  the storage was corrupted); then the app shows "Your saved trip data could
  not be loaded. Starting a new trip." and starts with an empty trip rather
  than crashing or silently discarding the data.

---

## S-9 — Start a new trip
**Serves:** J-1 | **Status:** Not implemented

As a Trip Treasurer, I want to clear all current trip data and start fresh,
so that I can use the app for a new trip without previous data interfering.

- Given the trip has participants and expenses; when I choose "Start new trip"
  and confirm; then the participant list and expense list are both empty and
  localStorage is cleared.
- Given I choose "Start new trip"; when I cancel at the confirmation prompt;
  then all participants and expenses remain intact.
- Given the trip is already empty; when I choose "Start new trip" and confirm;
  then the app remains on an empty state with no error.

---

## S-10 — View the settlement summary
**Serves:** J-3 | **Status:** Not implemented

As a Trip Treasurer, I want to see a labelled list of transfers that clears
all balances, so that the group knows exactly who pays whom and the trip is
fully settled.

**Normal cases:**
- Given Ali paid Rs. 600 for "Fuel" shared equally by Ali and Sara (each
  Rs. 300); then the settlement shows "Sara pays Ali Rs. 300".
- Given the Faisalabad scenario:
  - "Fuel to Faisalabad" Rs. 1,500, paid by Ali, shared by Ali and Usman
    (Rs. 750 each, no rounding)
  - "Fuel onwards" Rs. 2,000, paid by Usman, shared by Ali, Usman, Sara,
    Bilal (Rs. 500 each, no rounding)
  - "Hotel" Rs. 3,001, paid by Sara, shared by Ali, Usman, Sara, Bilal
    (Sara is payer and sharer — Sara Rs. 751, others Rs. 750 each per S-12)

  Net balances: Ali −Rs. 500, Usman Rs. 0, Sara +Rs. 1,750,
  Bilal −Rs. 1,250.

  Then the settlement shows: "Bilal pays Sara Rs. 1,250" and
  "Ali pays Sara Rs. 500".

- Given all net balances are zero; then the settlement shows "All balances
  are settled — no transfers needed."
- Given only one participant exists; then the settlement shows "All balances
  are settled — no transfers needed."

**Empty state:**
- Given no expenses have been added; when I view the settlement; then the app
  shows "No expenses have been added yet."

**Algorithm label:**
- The settlement section is headed "Simplified settlement" (not "Minimum
  transfers") to reflect that the greedy algorithm is not guaranteed to be
  the mathematical minimum.

**Mathematical invariant (verified by automated tests):**
- Given any set of valid expenses; when the settlement is computed; then
  applying all listed transfers to participants' net balances brings every
  balance to exactly Rs. 0.

**Continuation:**
- Given the settlement is displayed; when I add, edit or delete an expense;
  then the settlement recalculates automatically.

---

## S-11 — View the per-person breakdown
**Serves:** J-2, J-4 | **Status:** Not implemented

As a Trip Treasurer, I want to see a breakdown for each participant showing
the expenses they shared, their share of each, what they personally paid, and
their net balance, so that any group member can verify their own figure without
argument.

**Normal cases:**
- Given Ali paid Rs. 600 for "Fuel" (shared Ali, Sara — each Rs. 300), and
  Sara paid Rs. 900 for "Hotel" (shared Ali, Sara, Bilal — each Rs. 300);
  Ali's breakdown shows:
  - "Fuel": share Rs. 300, paid Rs. 600 → net from this expense: +Rs. 300
  - "Hotel": share Rs. 300, paid Rs. 0 → net from this expense: −Rs. 300
  - Summary: total paid Rs. 600, total owed Rs. 600, net balance Rs. 0
- Given Bilal was not on "Fuel"; then "Fuel" does not appear in Bilal's
  breakdown.
- Given Ali paid Rs. 300 for "Snacks" shared by Sara and Bilal only (Ali is
  payer but not a sharer); Ali's breakdown shows "Snacks": paid Rs. 300,
  share Rs. 0, net from this expense +Rs. 300.

**Consistency with settlement:**
- Given both the per-person breakdown and the settlement summary are
  displayed; then each participant's net balance in the breakdown matches
  exactly the net balance used in the settlement calculation.

**Zero balance:**
- Given a participant's total paid equals their total owed; then their
  breakdown shows net balance Rs. 0 and they do not appear in the settlement
  transfers.

*(Share values in the breakdown use the same rounded whole-rupee figures
defined in S-12.)*

---

## S-12 — See how each expense's shares were rounded
**Serves:** J-2, J-4 | **Status:** Not implemented

As a Trip Treasurer, I want to see, for each expense, how the total was
divided into whole-rupee shares and who absorbed the leftover, so that any
participant can confirm the rounding was consistent and fair.

### Canonical rounding rule
*(Referenced by S-4, S-5, S-10, S-11 — defined once here.)*

For an expense with total T (base + any rounded tip), payer P, and n sharers
listed in a fixed order:

**Case A — P is one of the n sharers:**
1. Every sharer except P receives ⌊T ÷ n⌋.
2. P receives T − (n − 1) × ⌊T ÷ n⌋. P absorbs the leftover.
3. Invariant: all n shares sum to T exactly.

**Case B — P is not one of the n sharers:**
1. Base share for each sharer: ⌊T ÷ n⌋.
2. Leftover = T − n × ⌊T ÷ n⌋ (between 0 and n − 1 rupees).
3. The first `leftover` sharers in listed order each receive one extra rupee.
4. Invariant: all n shares sum to T exactly.

**Tip rounding:** when a percentage tip is entered, the computed rupee amount
is rounded to the nearest whole rupee before being added to the base (halves
round up). The rounded total T is then divided as above.

**Shares always sum exactly to T in both cases.**

### Display placement

Rounding notes appear as a line beneath each expense in the expense list.
They are **not** repeated in the per-person breakdown (S-11).

### Zero-leftover rule

When leftover = 0 (the total divides evenly among all sharers), **no
rounding note is shown** — for both Case A and Case B.

### Acceptance criteria

**Case A — payer is a sharer:**
- Given Rs. 1,000, paid by Ali, shared by Ali → Sara → Bilal (listed order):
  Sara Rs. 333, Bilal Rs. 333, Ali Rs. 334 (absorbs Re. 1). Display shows
  "Ali absorbed Re. 1 rounding difference."
- Given Rs. 900, paid by Ali, shared by Ali → Sara → Bilal: each Rs. 300, no
  remainder. No rounding note shown.
- Given Rs. 1,001, paid by Ali, shared by Ali → Sara → Bilal: Sara Rs. 333,
  Bilal Rs. 333, Ali Rs. 335 (absorbs Rs. 2). Display shows "Ali absorbed
  Rs. 2 rounding difference."

**Case B — payer is not a sharer:**
- Given Rs. 1,000, paid by Ali (not sharing), shared by Sara → Bilal →
  Kamran: ⌊1000 ÷ 3⌋ = 333, leftover = 1. Sara Rs. 334, Bilal Rs. 333,
  Kamran Rs. 333. Sum = 1,000. Display shows "Re. 1 rounding difference added
  to Sara's share (first in listed order)."
- Given Rs. 1,001, paid by Ali (not sharing), shared by Sara → Bilal →
  Kamran: leftover = 2. Sara Rs. 334, Bilal Rs. 334, Kamran Rs. 333.
  Sum = 1,001. Display shows "Rs. 2 rounding difference distributed to Sara
  and Bilal (first in listed order)."
- Given Rs. 1,000, paid by Ali (not sharing), shared by Sara → Bilal only
  (2 sharers): 1000 ÷ 2 = 500 exactly. Sara Rs. 500, Bilal Rs. 500. No
  rounding note shown.

**Very small amounts:**
- Given Rs. 2, paid by Ali (not sharing), shared by Sara → Bilal → Kamran:
  ⌊2 ÷ 3⌋ = 0, leftover = 2. Sara Rs. 1, Bilal Rs. 1, Kamran Rs. 0.
  Sum = 2. Display shows "Rs. 2 rounding difference distributed to Sara and
  Bilal (first in listed order)." Kamran's share is Rs. 0 and still appears
  in the breakdown.

**With tip (Case A):**
- Given Rs. 1,000 + 10% tip = Rs. 1,100 total, paid by Ali (payer and
  sharer), shared by Ali → Sara → Bilal: ⌊1100 ÷ 3⌋ = 366, leftover = 2.
  Sara Rs. 366, Bilal Rs. 366, Ali Rs. 368. Display shows "Ali absorbed
  Rs. 2 rounding difference."

**Consistency:**
- The shares shown in S-12 are identical to those used in S-11 (per-person
  breakdown) and S-10 (settlement). There is one source of truth for rounding.

---

## "They must never" coverage

| Constraint from app-roles.md | Covered by |
|---|---|
| See a settlement where transfers do not account for every rupee of every net balance | S-10: mathematical invariant criterion |
| See shares on an expense that do not sum to the expense total including tip | S-12: invariant — shares sum exactly to T in both Case A and Case B |
| Lose entered data without an explicit confirmation step | S-7: delete confirmation; S-9: new-trip confirmation; S-8: corrupt-data message instead of silent discard |
| Remove a participant who is named on one or more expenses — app blocks and names the expenses | S-3: blocked-as-sharer, blocked-as-payer, multi-expense message |
| Submit an expense with no participants sharing it | S-4: "At least one participant must share this expense" |
| Enter a zero or negative expense amount | S-4: "Amount must be greater than zero" |
| Add a participant with an empty or duplicate name | S-1: empty-name and duplicate criteria; S-2: same on rename |
| Enter an amount that is not a whole number of rupees | S-4: "Amount must be a whole number of rupees"; S-5: "Tip must be a whole number of rupees" |
| Enter a single expense amount above Rs. 10,000,000 | S-4: boundary criteria; S-5: total-including-tip cap |
| Enter a negative tip, or a percentage tip above 100% | S-5: negative-tip and >100% criteria |

```markdown
# Trip Expense Splitter

A browser-based calculator that tracks shared expenses across a group trip and
produces a settlement showing who pays whom. Built as a take-home assignment
for KnowledgeCity (Technology Division).

---

## What it does and who it is for

**User:** The Trip Treasurer — one person who records shared expenses during or
after a group trip and needs to produce a final settlement the whole group can
trust.

**Problem it solves:** Multi-leg trips with variable group membership and
multiple payers produce a calculation that phone calculators and mental
arithmetic cannot handle reliably. For example: two legs with different
headcounts, each paid by a different person, with some participants on only one
leg — the net balance for each person and the minimum set of transfers is not
obvious.

**Why this calculator over others:** Dedicated expense-sharing apps require
accounts, app installs, and ongoing access. For a one-off group trip where a
single person is doing the bookkeeping, a purpose-built browser tool that runs
locally with no sign-up is faster to start and shares no data with any server.

**What you get:**

- A **simplified settlement** (greedy debtor-creditor matching): at most N − 1
  transfers, enough to clear every balance. Labelled "Simplified settlement"
  in the UI because the greedy result is not guaranteed to be the mathematical
  minimum — it is sufficient for typical group sizes of 3–8 people.
- A **per-person breakdown** showing each participant's share of every expense,
  what they paid, who they owe, and their net balance — so any group member can
  verify the numbers independently.

---

## Running the app

**Requirement:** Node 20 or later. No accounts, API keys, or cloud services.

```bash
npm install        # install dependencies (first time only)
npm run dev        # start dev server → open http://localhost:5173
```

### Unit tests

```bash
npm test           # runs once and exits (no watch mode)
```

### End-to-end tests

Requires a one-time Chromium download (~130 MB):

```bash
npx playwright install chromium   # one time only
npm run test:e2e                   # runs the full Playwright suite
```

`npm test` and `npm run test:e2e` are independent. Unit tests stay fast and
do not require a browser.

### Production build (optional)

```bash
npm run build      # outputs to dist/
npm run preview    # serve the production build locally
```

---

## How it was verified

| Layer | Tool | Count |
|---|---|---|
| Pure logic (rounding, balances, settlement, storage) | Vitest unit tests | 95 tests |
| Full UI and user flows | Playwright E2E (Chromium) | 83 tests |
| Manual walkthroughs | 10 scenarios in `docs/qa-checklist.md` | all Pass — Chrome, 2026-10-19 |

Every story marked Implemented in `docs/user-stories.md` is covered by at
least one automated test and at least one passed manual scenario.

---

## AI tools used

| Tool | Role |
|---|---|
| Claude Code CLI (claude-sonnet-4-6) | Wrote all code, tests, and documentation under PM direction |
| Claude Desktop | Used to generate and cross-verify discovery prompts for session 01 |

All code was written by the AI. The PM (assignment author) directed each step,
reviewed outputs, caught bugs, and confirmed acceptance criteria by hand.

---

## Manual code changes

None. All changes were made through Claude Code under explicit PM instruction.
If any hand-edits are made after submission, they will be logged here.

---

## Assumptions and scope

### In scope

- Add, rename, remove participants (with guard: cannot remove someone on an
  expense).
- Add, edit, delete expenses: description, amount (whole rupees), payer, subset
  of sharers.
- Optional tip per expense: percentage or flat rupee amount, added before
  splitting.
- localStorage persistence: survives tab close and browser restart on the same
  device and browser.
- New Trip: clears all data after explicit confirmation.
- Simplified settlement (greedy, ≤ N − 1 transfers).
- Per-person breakdown with "Paid by" column for auditability.

### Rounding rule (S-12)

All shares are whole rupees. For total T, payer P, n sharers in listed order:

- **Case A — P is a sharer:** every other sharer gets ⌊T ÷ n⌋; P absorbs the
  remainder. Example: Rs. 1,000 ÷ 3 → others Rs. 333, payer Rs. 334.
- **Case B — P is not a sharer:** base share ⌊T ÷ n⌋; leftover rupees
  distributed one each to the first sharers in listed order. Example:
  Rs. 1,000 paid by Ali (not sharing), 3 sharers → Sara Rs. 334, others
  Rs. 333.
- Percentage tip rounds to the nearest whole rupee (halves round up) before
  splitting.
- A rounding note appears under the expense in the list when leftover > 0.
  No note when the total divides evenly.

### Out of scope

| Feature | Reason excluded |
|---|---|
| Custom per-item splits | Multiplies edge-case complexity; outside time budget |
| Cross-device sync | Requires a backend; forbidden by reviewer constraint |
| Multi-currency | Requires a live exchange-rate API |
| User accounts, group invites, payment reminders | Require a backend |
| Receipt photo / OCR | Requires a vision API |
| Ongoing household ledger | Wrong shape for a one-trip tool |

### Known limitations (assumptions from discovery)

- **A1** — Data is entered on one device and browser. Clearing browser storage
  or switching device loses the trip.
- **A2** — One person enters all data (no simultaneous multi-user input).
- **A3** — Equal-per-participant splitting only; item-level custom weights are
  out of scope for v1.
- **A4** — Users who already use a dedicated expense-sharing app are unlikely
  to switch for a single trip.
- **A5** — Greedy settlement (≤ N − 1 transfers) is acceptable; not the
  mathematical minimum.
- **A6** — All amounts are in Pakistani Rupees; no multi-currency support.

---

| `docs/assignment-brief.md` | Original brief from KnowledgeCity |
| `docs/app-roles.md` | Two app roles: Trip Treasurer and Trip Participant |
| `docs/jobs-to-be-done.md` | Four jobs-to-be-done (J-1 through J-4) |

# Trip Expense Splitter

A browser-based calculator that tracks shared expenses across a group trip and produces a settlement showing who pays whom. Built as a take-home assignment for KnowledgeCity (Technology Division).

---

## Running the app

**Requirements:** Node 20 or later. No accounts, API keys or cloud services needed.

```bash
npm install      # install dependencies (first time only)
npm run dev      # start local dev server → open http://localhost:5173
```

### Running tests

```bash
npm test         # run unit tests once and exit
```

### End-to-end tests

E2E tests require a one-time browser download (about 130 MB for Chromium):

```bash
npx playwright install chromium
```

Then:

```bash
npm run test:e2e    # runs the full Playwright suite
```

`npm test` (unit tests) and `npm run test:e2e` are independent — `npm test` stays fast and does not require a browser.

E2E tests run against `npm run dev` (auto-started by Playwright). They cover all acceptance criteria that are practical to automate. The 10 scenarios in `docs/qa-checklist.md` cover the remainder (genuine browser restart, cross-browser visual checks).

### Production build (optional)

```bash
npm run build    # outputs to dist/
npm run preview  # serve the production build locally
```

---

## What it does

Add trip participants, record shared expenses (who paid, who shares, optional tip), and get:

- A **simplified settlement** listing who pays whom to clear all debts.
- A **per-person breakdown** showing each participant's share of every expense, what they paid, and their net balance — so anyone can verify the numbers.

Data is saved automatically to the browser's local storage. Closing the tab and reopening restores your trip. Use **New Trip** to clear everything and start again.

---

## Key assumptions

The following assumptions were made during discovery (no real user interviews were conducted):

- **A1** — Users enter expenses on the same device and browser throughout the trip. Data survives tab closure; it does not survive clearing browser storage or switching device.
- **A2** — One person acts as treasurer and does all data entry. Simultaneous multi-user input is not supported.
- **A3** — Equal-per-participant splitting is the dominant rule. Item-level splits within a single bill are out of scope for v1.
- **A4** — Users prefer a purpose-built browser tool over a phone calculator for multi-expense trips. This is the core adoption risk: users who feel enough pain may already use dedicated expense-sharing apps, and those who don't may not adopt a new tool either.
- **A5** — Greedy settlement (≤ N−1 transfers) is acceptable. Users do not need a mathematically optimal minimum.
- **A6** — All amounts are in Pakistani Rupees. No multi-currency support.

---

## Manual changes

*None so far. If you edit code by hand, log the change here with a date and description.*

---

## Architecture

```
src/
  logic/          Pure TypeScript — no DOM, fully unit tested
    types.ts      Domain types (Participant, Expense, TipInput, …)
    validation.ts Input validation (returns error strings or null)
    tip.ts        Tip calculation and percentage rounding
    rounding.ts   Whole-rupee share splitting (S-12 canonical rule)
    balances.ts   Net balance computation per participant
    settlement.ts Greedy debtor-creditor settlement algorithm
    storage.ts    localStorage load/save (takes a StorageBackend parameter)
  ui/
    state.ts      App state singleton
    utils.ts      escHtml, formatRs, newId
    app.ts        Render loop + all event handlers
    sections/     One file per UI section (render + bind)
  main.ts         Entry point
  style.css       Styles
```

The logic layer has zero DOM access and zero side effects. All calculation functions take plain data in and return plain data out. Storage takes a `StorageBackend` interface so tests can use an in-memory fake.
